Requirements: A complete application includes: Application form, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, CV/Resumé, Official GRE General Test scores, Official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores (international applicants only), Application fee
Description: The Master of Arts in Quantitative Economics is a two-year program designed for students who want to develop strong analytical and quantitative skills for careers in finance, economics, business, and data science. The program helps students apply these skills to solve problems in these fields. The program also serves as a stepping stone for students who want to pursue a PhD in economics and other quantitatively oriented fields. The MA in Quantitative Economics is a STEM-designated program.
ScholarshipAmount: Full-tuition scholarship (valued at $67,100 per year) plus a stipend for Teaching Fellowships; 25% to 75% of tuition for Dean's Scholarships.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Dean's Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Editorial Studies
Requirements: All applicants should submit the following: Application Form, Application Fee, Transcripts, Three Letters of Recommendation, Personal Statement, GRE General Test (optional for Fall 2024 applicants to all MA, MS, and PhD programs in GRS), English Proficiency Examination, Writing Sample, Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume.
Description: The MA in Editorial Studies offers intensive study in the history and theory of editing, and in the history of the book and print culture. Students acquire practical editorial experience through work on the papers of leading American literary figures, philosophers, and statesmen in the internationally known Boston University Stone Arch Initiatives. Students take courses both in the Editorial Institute and in relevant departments within the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. These courses typically focus on American literature, American history, and American studies, but may also include study of relevant European figures and movements. The program is excellent preparation for doctoral study in such fields as American literature, English literature, history, and American studies. Its unique combination of historical and practical work also qualifies graduates for positions in scholarly publishing.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (GRS Scholarship), Teaching Fellowship, Research Assistantship

ProgramName: PhD in Editorial Studies
Requirements: All applicants to the PhD in Editorial Studies program must submit the following materials through the GRS online application: Transcripts from all institutions where you received a degree; Three letters of recommendation; Statement of Purpose; Writing Sample; Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume; GRE General Test; English Proficiency (if applicable).
Description: The Editorial Institute at Boston University is dedicated to editing and the history of the book. It offers an interdisciplinary PhD in Editorial Studies through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Editorial Studies provides students with skills in textual scholarship and analytical bibliography, as well as an opportunity to gain experience in practical editing. Graduates are prepared for careers in higher education and other professions. The Institute welcomes inquiries from students in all fields of literary, historical, and philosophical study, especially those with a research interest in the theory and practice of scholarly editing.
ScholarshipType: Full-tuition scholarship, Stipends, Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in English
Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Arts (MA) program in English should apply online through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS). A complete application includes: Application for Admission (online application), Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores (The GRE General Test is required), English Proficiency (for international students), Application Fee. A writing sample is also required.
Description: The MA in English program prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, publishing, writing, and the arts, as well as for further study in a PhD program. The MA curriculum emphasizes depth and rigor across a broad range of Anglophone literatures and cultures, while giving students the opportunity to focus on particular areas of interest by selecting courses from a wide array of offerings across literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches. Students gain experience in literary research, critical methodology, and written and oral communication, culminating in a final research paper or project.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based fellowships, Dean's Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Course Assistantships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Arts / Juris Doctor in English
Requirements: Applicants for the JD/MA program must apply separately to the School of Law and to the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS). Law School applications require transcripts, a personal statement, a resume, and letters of recommendation. For the MA in English, applicants apply to the GRS through the English Department and should follow the instructions for MA applicants. This application requires transcripts, a personal statement, a writing sample, and letters of recommendation.
Department: Boston University School of Law and Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) Department of English
Description: Boston University’s English MA program offers rigorous training in literary and cultural studies. Our curriculum covers the historical range of British and American literature while also fostering students’ engagement with various theoretical and methodological approaches and contemporary debates in the field. Students benefit from the program’s proximity to Boston’s rich literary history, its many cultural institutions, and its dynamic intellectual life. Our MA prepares students for PhD work, careers in secondary education, or further professional training in fields like law, business, and journalism.

ProgramName: PhD in English
Requirements: Applications should include: a statement of purpose outlining your intellectual interests, academic background, and future goals; (1000 words or less); a critical writing sample (15-25 pages, double-spaced) that demonstrates your analytical skills and ability to construct a sustained argument; three letters of recommendation from faculty members familiar with your academic work; transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions; GRE scores (the English Subject Test is not required); the general GRE is optional for Fall 2024 admissions. International students must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores unless they have or will receive a degree from a US or English-speaking university. A CV or resume may be submitted, but is not required. The application fee.
Description: The PhD in English and American Literature prepares students for careers as scholars and teachers of literature, with an emphasis on research-intensive positions in higher education. Students develop their understanding of a wide range of literatures in English and critical theories, hone their skills as researchers and writers, and gain experience in the classroom through teaching opportunities in the Writing Program and the English Department. Students pursuing the PhD typically earn the MA in English and American Literature en route to the doctorate, which can be completed in five to six years. Our PhD is a fully funded program, which includes an annual stipend, a tuition scholarship, and a health insurance contribution. Students in the PhD program receive five years of funding, normally distributed as three years of Teaching Fellowship and two years of Scholarship or Fellowship.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in History
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in history or a related field. General requirements for admission include an online application form, application fee, transcripts from all previous colleges and universities, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a writing sample. The GRE General Test is optional for all GRS MA and PhD programs. English proficiency scores may be required for international applicants.
Description:
The MA Program in History is designed primarily to provide students with a solid grounding in the discipline of history while also allowing them to pursue their own areas of historical interest. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a number of professional careers as well as for further graduate study at the PhD level.

Program Learning Outcomes
*   Demonstrate knowledge of historical debates and historiographical traditions, especially within their fields of specialization.
*   Formulate a historical problem and develop an original argument, supported by evidence, in the form of a research paper or essay.
*   Carry out historical research, using both primary and secondary sources.
*   Communicate historical arguments clearly and effectively in both written and oral form.
*   Acquire professional skills appropriate for historians working in a variety of settings.

ProgramName: PhD in History
Master of Arts in History of Art & Architecture
Requirements: Admission to the MA program in History of Art & Architecture is highly competitive. Decisions are based on a combination of factors, including: Undergraduate record (particularly in art history and related fields), Statement of purpose, Writing sample, Letters of recommendation, GRE scores are not required for MA applicants.
Description: The MA Program in the History of Art & Architecture at Boston University provides students with a broad and deep foundation in the methods, theories, and history of art and architectural history, while also allowing for specialization based on a student’s interests. Graduates of the program are prepared for doctoral work in art and architectural history, for museum work, and for a variety of professions that benefit from training in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. The program emphasizes both breadth and depth in students’ training. They take introductory courses in theory and methods, and also choose courses across different chronological periods and geographical areas from our diverse faculty. While the coursework ensures that students gain knowledge of a wide range of fields, students also select a major and minor field of specialization for their comprehensive exams and master’s thesis. The mission of Boston University’s MA Program in the History of Art & Architecture is to train students in the methods and theories of art and architectural history, provide them with a broad understanding of the field, and support their development of specialized knowledge in preparation for a range of professional futures, including doctoral study, museum work, and other careers requiring advanced skills in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. Upon completion of the program, students will: Demonstrate knowledge of the methods, theories, and historiography of art and architectural history; Develop specialized knowledge of at least two fields within art and architectural history and their respective scholarly traditions; Formulate an original research project based on a critical engagement with existing scholarship and primary sources; Present research effectively in written and oral forms; Teach confidently and effectively at the college level.
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Assistantships, Tuition Scholarships, Dean's Scholarships for Excellence in Graduate Study

ProgramName: Master of Arts / Juris Doctor in History of Art & Architecture
Requirements: Applicants must apply separately and be accepted to both the School of Law and the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS). The JD application requires an Application Form, Personal Statement, Resume, LSAC Credential Assembly Service (CAS) Report (which includes academic transcripts, letters of recommendation, and an LSAT score), LSAT Score, Character and Fitness, and Application Fee. The MA in History of Art & Architecture application requires official transcripts, a current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV), a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, a writing sample (an essay or excerpt from a longer work, ideally on a topic in art history or architectural history, no more than 20 pages in length, excluding bibliography), and an application fee. GRE General Test scores are not required for applicants to the MA in History of Art & Architecture.
Department: School of Law and College of Arts & Sciences
Fees.1: Annual tuition for the School of Law is $70,880 (2024-2025). Additional annual fees for Law School include $1,478 (Law School Fees), $440 (Health & Wellness Fee), and $3,604 (Health Insurance). For semesters where dual degree students are enrolled only in courses outside the School of Law, tuition will be charged at the College of Arts & Sciences graduate rate ($32,960/semester for full-time or $1,030/credit for part-time).
Description: Students may pursue a dual degree in law and the history of art and architecture, in conjunction with the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. The MA/JD in History of Art & Architecture prepares students to work with public and private collections, museums, and institutions involved in the law of art, cultural heritage, and historic preservation. The program is designed for completion within four years.

ProgramName: PhD in History of Art & Architecture
Requirements: The department offers admission for the MA and PhD degrees. All applicants for admission to the MA and PhD programs in History of Art & Architecture must apply through the Boston University Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS). The application for Fall 2024 opened in September 2023. Required Application Materials for MA and PhD programs include: Online Application, Personal Statement, Curriculum Vitae (CV), Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, Writing Sample, English Proficiency Examination (if applicable). The GRE General Test is not required.
Department: College of Arts & Sciences, Department of History of Art & Architecture
Fees: Admitted PhD students receive a full-tuition scholarship and a stipend. A PhD continuation fee of $425 per semester applies after the first two semesters of full-time enrollment.
Fees.1: Gross full-time tuition for GRS (2024-2025) is $33,540/semester or $67,080/year. Admitted PhD students receive a full-tuition scholarship covering this amount.
Description:
The Ph.D. program in the History of Art & Architecture is a highly selective and rigorous course of study designed to prepare students for careers as scholars and teachers of art and architectural history. We offer a comprehensive curriculum, with courses in areas ranging from ancient to contemporary art, and from the history of architecture to the history of photography. Through our program, students develop a mastery of art history, hone their research skills, deepen their understanding of theory and methodology, gain significant teaching experience, and participate in a vibrant intellectual community of faculty and students. In all these ways, our Ph.D. program prepares students to enter the profession with confidence and to make significant contributions to the field.

The department’s Ph.D. program is distinguished by its intimate size, encouraging close mentorship of students by faculty. Small classes and regular opportunities for informal exchange foster a strong sense of intellectual community. Our students are deeply involved in the life of the department, contributing to our speaker series and conferences, as well as to our undergraduate journal, Lux. The faculty is a community of outstanding scholars and award-winning teachers whose work spans a wide range of fields, methodologies, and critical approaches to the history of art and architecture. Our faculty members have active research programs in various fields including ancient, medieval, renaissance, baroque, eighteenth- and nineteenth-century European, American, Latin American, East Asian, and modern and contemporary art and architecture, as well as the history of photography.

All of our Ph.D. students are fully funded for five years, with an annual stipend and full tuition remission. Students also receive excellent training and experience as university teachers, typically beginning in their second year. During their second through fourth years, students gain valuable pedagogical experience by teaching sections of our large introductory lecture courses, with oversight and mentoring by the faculty member of record. Advanced doctoral students, after passing their qualifying exams, may also have the opportunity to teach their own introductory courses.

We encourage prospective applicants to contact faculty members whose research interests align with their own.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition ($67,080/Year gross) plus a stipend of $27,000/Year

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Relations
Requirements: The Mid-Career MA in International Relations is designed for professionals with a minimum of seven years of full-time, relevant work experience in the international relations field. In addition to work experience, successful applicants will demonstrate strong academic preparation. To apply for the Mid-Career MA, submit an application through the Boston University Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) and all supporting materials, including: Academic Transcripts, Personal Statement, Three Letters of Recommendation, GRE Score (optional), CV / Résumé, Writing Sample, English Language Proficiency (international students only), Application Fee.
Description: Boston University’s accelerated Mid-Career Master of Arts (MA) in International Relations program provides a robust, immersive, and intellectually rigorous curriculum for working professionals and individuals with substantial career experience. The MA in International Relations Mid-Career is designed for students seeking to advance existing careers, change career trajectories, or deepen their understanding of international affairs. This distinctive degree is completed in one academic year and prepares students for a diverse range of careers in diplomacy, government, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: PhD in International Relations
Requirements: Submit the GRS online application, official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose (1500 words maximum), a writing sample (20 pages maximum), the GRE General Test, English Proficiency (for international students whose native language is not English and whose undergraduate degree is from an institution in a country where English is not the official language), a current CV or resume, and an $85 non-refundable application fee.
Description: The Pardee School PhD program in International Relations provides a small number of exceptional students with a rigorous, interdisciplinary, and policy-relevant education appropriate for careers as scholars and practitioners in international affairs. The program is designed to develop students’ analytic, research, and communication skills through a flexible curriculum that enables them to conduct original, cutting-edge research and successfully launch their careers in academia, government, or the private sector. Upon completion of the PhD in International Relations, students will be able to: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of major theories, issues, and research methods in international relations; Conduct original, independent research that contributes to scholarship in international relations; Clearly and effectively communicate research findings, both orally and in writing, to scholarly and policy audiences.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition + living stipend + health insurance credit
ScholarshipType: Full-tuition scholarship, living stipend, health insurance credit

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Latin American Studies
Requirements: The following materials are required for the application process: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation. A Statement of Purpose of 500–1000 words in length outlining academic interests and goals. GRE scores are not required. Official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores if applicable. A writing sample in English (10–20 pages in length). The sample should demonstrate your research and analytical abilities. Non-refundable fee of $85. A CV or resume.
Description: The MA in Latin American Studies (M.A.L.A.S.) is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students a comprehensive understanding of Latin America. Students are able to combine courses in the humanities and social sciences across BU departments to pursue their interests in the politics, history, societies, and cultures of Latin America. The MA program provides excellent preparation for further graduate study in a doctoral program or for a career in government, NGOs, international organizations, journalism, or business.

ProgramName: PhD in Latin American Studies
Requirements: Candidates for admission to the PhD in Latin American Studies program must satisfy the general requirements for graduate admission at Boston University. The online application is managed through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) and includes the following:
Department: Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies within the College of Arts & Sciences
Description: Students who pursue a PhD in Latin American Studies apply to, and are admitted by, one of Boston University’s disciplinary departments (e.g., Anthropology, History, Modern Languages and Comparative Literature, Political Science, Sociology). Students in the PhD program focus their disciplinary research on Latin America and complete the requirements for the PhD in Latin American Studies in addition to the requirements of their disciplinary department. Admission to the PhD program is highly competitive; therefore, applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic performance at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. All PhD students are fully funded, normally for five years, through a combination of stipends and tuition scholarships. For more information, please contact LAS. A full description of the requirements can be found in the Graduate Guide.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Linguistics
Requirements: A complete application includes: a completed application form, official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a writing sample, a resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV), and an application fee. For international students, English proficiency scores (TOEFL, IELTS) are required if applicable. The GRE General Test is not required for applicants to the MA in Linguistics.
Description: The MA in Linguistics is a two-year course of study leading to a thesis. It is designed to prepare students for doctoral study, and for careers requiring expertise in linguistics. The program offers comprehensive training in linguistic theory, research methods, and descriptive linguistics, with a strong emphasis on computational and experimental linguistics. Students develop a deep understanding of the structure and function of language, and gain hands-on experience in research and analysis. Graduates are well-prepared for PhD programs in linguistics or related fields, as well as positions in industry and government that require strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
ScholarshipType: Research assistantships, Teaching fellowships, Dean’s Scholarships

ProgramName: PhD in Linguistics
Requirements: The PhD in Linguistics program at Boston University prepares students for careers in research and teaching at universities and other institutions. Successful applicants to the PhD program typically have a strong undergraduate record, including significant coursework in linguistics or a related field, and evidence of research potential. Applicants are encouraged to contact individual faculty whose research interests align with their own. Applications are submitted through the GRS online application portal. Required Application Materials: Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts from all post-secondary institutions. Official transcripts will be required upon admission and matriculation. Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation from faculty members or others qualified to evaluate academic potential. Statement of Purpose: A 500-1000 word essay describing your reasons for pursuing graduate study, your academic and research interests, and your future goals. Writing Sample: A scholarly paper, such as a term paper, thesis chapter, or published article (maximum 30 pages). Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume: A current CV or resume detailing your academic history, research experience, publications, presentations, and any relevant work experience. GRE General Test Scores: The GRE General Test is optional for applicants to the PhD in Linguistics program. If you choose to submit scores, they should be sent directly from ETS to Boston University, institution code 3087. English Proficiency: International applicants for whom English is not their native language must submit official scores from the TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, or Duolingo English Test, unless they have completed a bachelor’s or graduate degree at an institution where the primary language of instruction was English. Refer to the GRS English Proficiency Requirements for more information. Application Fee: Please consult the GRS Admissions page for information on the application fee and fee waivers.
Description: The Department of Linguistics offers a PhD program in Linguistics. The goal of the PhD program is to provide students with a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics and to prepare them to conduct independent research in the field. We offer courses and research opportunities in all of the main theoretical areas of linguistics, including phonology, phonetics, syntax, semantics, and pragmatics, as well as in areas such as psycholinguistics, computational linguistics, historical linguistics, field methods, and language acquisition. Our students are trained to develop their own original research programs and to contribute to the advancement of linguistic theory. They also have opportunities to gain experience in teaching and to participate in interdisciplinary research projects. Most students admitted to the PhD program receive five years of funding, covering tuition and health insurance, plus a stipend in return for teaching duties and/or research assistantships. Exceptional students may be considered for merit fellowships which do not have teaching or research requirements. Students complete coursework and examinations in the core areas of linguistics, conduct original research, and write a dissertation. The program culminates in the defense of the dissertation. Students typically complete the program in 5–6 years. For more information about specific program requirements, see the GRS Bulletin.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Literary Translation
Requirements:
Applicants to the MFA in Literary Translation should hold a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. They must submit the following materials to the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences through the online application portal:
*   Application for Admission
*   Transcripts
*   Three Letters of Recommendation
*   Statement of Purpose outlining your academic objectives, reasons for wishing to pursue the MFA in Literary Translation, and career goals.
*   Writing Sample of a literary translation, accompanied by the original text. The length of the sample should not exceed 10 pages. We encourage applicants to choose a sample that showcases their strengths in both translation and literary analysis. For more information regarding writing sample submissions, please consult the GRS website.
*   English-language writing sample (critical essay, fiction, or poetry) of 10–15 pages. This sample demonstrates your writing ability in English and your potential as a literary artist.
*   Curriculum Vitae or Résumé
*   Proof of English Proficiency if applicable
Description: The Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Literary Translation is a two-year, 48-credit program based in the Editorial Institute. It offers an intensive course of study in literary translation for students who aim to develop their skills and knowledge as professional translators. The program combines academic training in translation theory and history with practical experience in various genres and styles. Students work closely with faculty mentors, many of whom are accomplished translators and scholars, and engage with a vibrant community of writers and translators in Boston and beyond. The MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous curriculum designed to cultivate highly skilled and reflective translators. Students delve into the nuances of language, culture, and literary style, gaining expertise in translating poetry, prose, and drama. The program emphasizes a hands-on approach, with workshops focused on practical translation techniques, editing, and revision. In addition to core translation courses, students explore relevant fields such as comparative literature, linguistics, and publishing. The curriculum culminates in a substantial translation project, often publishable quality, accompanied by a critical introduction.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Chinese/Literary Translation
Requirements: Please refer to the GRS Admissions page for more information about the application process and required materials. The general GRS application checklist includes: A completed application form; Application fee; Personal statement/statement of purpose; Three letters of recommendation; Official academic transcripts; GRE General Test results (not required for all programs; check your program’s website); English proficiency examination results; Writing sample (for certain programs only; check your program’s website); Resume/CV (for certain programs only; check your program’s website).
Description: Offered by the Department of Literatures in English and Romance Studies, the MFA in Literary Translation at Boston University is a two-year, full-time program. The MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous curriculum in literary translation and translation studies, leading to the completion of a book-length translation into English from one of many source languages. Students may specialize in translation from a range of languages into English, including Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Latin, Modern Greek, Polish, Russian, and Spanish. The program is designed for students interested in careers as literary translators, editors, and scholars. It is ideally suited for those seeking to combine the practical application of translating with the study of translation theory and history.
ScholarshipType: Dean’s Scholarships, Departmental Fellowships and Scholarships, Teaching Assistantships, Research Assistantships

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Comparative Literature/Literary Translation
Requirements: Minimum of a BA degree from an accredited institution. Unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Two letters of recommendation. International students whose native language is not English and who have not completed a degree at an institution in the US, Canada, the United Kingdom, or Australia must demonstrate English proficiency through either the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test. Visit the GRS Admissions page for more details.
Description: The MFA in Literary Translation is a terminal degree that provides an intensive course of study in translation practice, theory, and history. Students in the MFA program receive training in comparative literary studies while developing their skills as literary translators. The MFA requires a total of 32 credits (eight courses) and a translation thesis submitted in the final semester. Students generally complete the program in two years. With faculty guidance, students develop their individual interests and create a translation portfolio and a substantial thesis, often of publishable quality. They emerge from the program prepared for a career as a professional translator, or for further graduate study in comparative literature, literary translation, or a related field. The MFA degree is housed in the Department of Comparative Literature.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Boston University Fellowships, Graduate Research Assistantships, Teaching Fellowships, Dean's Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in French Studies/Literary Translation
Requirements: Admission to the MFA program is based on the quality of an applicant’s writing, previous academic record, letters of recommendation, and evidence of proficiency in English and at least one other language. Applicants are required to submit official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work, a statement of purpose, a writing sample, and three letters of recommendation. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for this program. Applicants whose native language is not English and who have not received a bachelor’s or master’s degree from a university in the United States, Canada, Great Britain, Australia, or New Zealand must also submit official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores.
Description: The MFA in Literary Translation is a two-year program for students of exceptional linguistic and literary talent. The program is designed to provide students with thorough training in the practice of literary translation as well as a solid grounding in translation studies, literary history and theory, and comparative literature. Students are expected to complete a thesis consisting of a book-length literary translation accompanied by an introduction and footnotes. The program has a strong international focus and includes a number of opportunities for students to study abroad, including a summer course in Venice, Italy, and exchange programs with universities in Geneva, Switzerland; Leuven, Belgium; and Shanghai, China.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowship (Merit-based, includes tuition scholarship and living stipend)

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in German/Literary Translation
Requirements: Applicants apply through the Boston University Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) online application system. General GRS requirements include official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, English proficiency testing (international students only), three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose (approximately 500 words), and a current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV). Program-specific requirements for the MFA in Literary Translation include a writing sample of 10–15 pages of original creative or critical writing (a portion of which should be a literary translation into English, accompanied by the original source text), and native or near-native fluency in English and at least one other language.
Description: The Boston University Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in Literary Translation is a two-year, 48-credit program that includes study in the theory and practice of literary translation, as well as the translation of literary texts from a foreign language into English. Students may specialize in Chinese, French, German, Japanese, and Spanish. Graduates are prepared for careers as literary translators, editors, and publishers, as well as for further study in a PhD program. The program provides an opportunity for students to refine their own work through workshops; to participate in the translation community through various conferences, talks, and campus visits by writers and translators; to gain experience in literary publishing; and to develop their own critical and historical understanding of the art of translation.
ScholarshipType: Tuition scholarships, stipends, graduate assistantships, teaching fellowships, Dean’s Scholarships

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Japanese/Literary Translation
Requirements: We encourage applicants from a wide range of academic backgrounds to apply. Admission to the MFA in Japanese/Literary Translation program is competitive. Applicants should demonstrate high potential for creative work in literary translation, critical and analytical ability, and fluency in both Japanese and English. In addition to the online application form, the following materials are required: Three letters of recommendation. Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions. A personal statement. A writing sample: an essay or paper, approximately 10–15 pages in length, demonstrating your critical and analytical abilities. An additional writing sample: your translation of a short literary text from Japanese into English, approximately 5–7 pages in length, with the original Japanese text appended. No GRE General Test required. For international students, TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores are required.
Description: Our MFA program in Literary Translation provides a rigorous professional training in the theory and practice of literary translation in several languages, primarily from French, German, Italian, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, and Japanese. The program emphasizes an informed, critical approach to literary translation, grounded in a close reading of texts and an understanding of the cultural and historical contexts in which they arise. Working closely with active literary translators, students develop professional skills through hands-on practice, translation workshops, translation theory courses, and directed individual studies that culminate in the production of a book-length translation and the professional portfolio required for entry into the field. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers as literary translators, editors, and scholars, and for further doctoral work in comparative literature or related fields.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition for 32 credits (total program credits), plus stipend and health insurance
ScholarshipType: Tuition scholarship, Teaching Fellowship, Research Assistantship

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Spanish/Literary Translation
Requirements:
This accelerated program allows eligible Boston University undergraduates to earn both a BA in Spanish and an MFA in Literary Translation. Students apply to the MFA program in their junior year at BU by completing the standard MFA application for the BU Graduate School of Arts & Sciences during the fall of their junior year, indicating their interest in the accelerated degree program.

Eligibility for the Combined BA/MFA Program:
1.  Students must have completed 72 credits by the time they apply, including courses to be completed in the fall semester of the junior year.
2.  Students must have a GPA of 3.3 or higher overall and a GPA of 3.5 or higher in Spanish and related courses.
3.  Applicants must be making satisfactory progress toward the BA in Spanish and must complete all BA requirements to continue into the MFA portion of the program.
4.  Students must have completed CAS LS 350 and LS 351 by the time of application or be enrolled in both during the semester of application.
5.  Students must identify a faculty advisor in Literary Translation who will work with them as they prepare their writing sample.

General application materials for the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences include:
*   Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
*   Three letters of recommendation.
*   A statement of purpose (approximately 500–750 words).
*   A resume or curriculum vitae.
*   GRE General Test (optional for most Master's and PhD programs in the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences for the 2024–2025 and 2025–2026 application cycles).
*   TOEFL/IELTS Scores (required for international applicants, unless exempt).
*   An $85 application fee.
Description: The BA in Spanish + MFA in Literary Translation is a five-year program that prepares students for careers in translation while offering a firm grounding in the liberal arts. The program provides the linguistic, cultural, and literary knowledge essential for high-level work in literary translation. Through coursework and supervised practice, students hone the analytical skills required to produce publishable translations in a variety of fields, from fiction and poetry to academic prose and commercial texts. The program is ideal for students with advanced Spanish language skills and a strong interest in literature and writing. Graduates of the program are well-prepared to pursue careers in publishing, international relations, education, and other fields that require advanced linguistic and intercultural competence.
AverageScholarshipAmount: ~95200/Year (covers full tuition and living stipend for 2024-2025 academic year)
ScholarshipAmount: ~95200/Year (covers full tuition and living stipend for 2024-2025 academic year)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Mathematics & Statistics
Requirements: All applicants must supply: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation. Statement of purpose. A non-refundable application fee. Applicants from countries where English is not the official language must take the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test. While GRE scores are not explicitly required, applicants are encouraged to submit them if they feel the scores would strengthen their application.
Department: Boston University College of Arts & Sciences
Description: The MA in Mathematics & Statistics is intended for students who want to strengthen their mathematical background and prepare for a PhD in mathematics or statistics, or for those who wish to pursue a career that involves significant mathematical or statistical knowledge. The program offers flexibility, allowing students to tailor their courses to fit their individual interests and career goals. Students choose courses from across a wide range of fields in mathematics and statistics, including pure and applied mathematics, probability, mathematical statistics, computational statistics, and data science. The program can be completed in two to four semesters of full-time study.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Assistantships, GRS Fellowships, External Fellowships, Federal Financial Aid

ProgramName: PhD in Mathematics & Statistics
Requirements: Official Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Resume/CV, GRE General Test Scores (optional for Fall 2024 applicants), GRE Subject Test (Mathematics) Scores (optional), English Proficiency (if applicable), Application Fee.
Description: The Department of Mathematics & Statistics at Boston University offers the PhD in Mathematics & Statistics. Our doctoral program is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of advanced mathematical and statistical concepts, as well as the research skills necessary to contribute new knowledge to the field. Through rigorous coursework, comprehensive exams, and original dissertation research, students prepare for careers in academia, industry, and government. Our faculty are active researchers in a wide range of mathematical and statistical disciplines, providing students with diverse opportunities for mentorship and collaboration. The program emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, encouraging students to engage with real-world problems. We strive to develop independent scholars capable of critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication of complex ideas.
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition scholarship (valued at $69,880/Year) plus a stipend of $35,000 for 9 months.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Tuition Scholarship, Stipend, Health Insurance Subsidy

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: Applicants to the MA in Mathematics program come from a wide variety of undergraduate backgrounds. Successful applicants typically have a solid background in undergraduate mathematics, including courses in real analysis (at the level of MA 511), complex analysis, abstract algebra, and topology. In addition, successful applicants typically have taken courses in advanced calculus and linear algebra. It is not necessary to have majored in mathematics; applicants with majors in other fields, such as computer science, engineering, and economics, are welcome to apply if they have taken the necessary mathematics courses. All applicants to the MA in Mathematics program must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended; Two letters of recommendation; A statement of purpose; GRE General Test scores are not required for applicants to the MA in Mathematics program; English proficiency test scores (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo) are required if your native language is not English. If you have completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree at an institution where the primary language of instruction is English, you are exempt from this requirement; Application fee.
Description: The MA in Mathematics program is intended for students with a strong background in mathematics who wish to deepen their mathematical knowledge and pursue further study in mathematics or a related field, or to pursue a career in teaching or in a field requiring advanced mathematical skills. Students completing the MA in Mathematics program will have a solid foundation in the core areas of analysis and algebra and will have the opportunity to take advanced courses in a variety of other areas of mathematics. The MA program provides an excellent background for students considering doctoral studies in mathematics. The program can be completed in one or two years depending on the student’s background and course load.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Statistical Practice
Requirements:
For all graduate programs in the Department of Mathematics & Statistics, applicants must follow the general GRS Application Guidelines. Specific information regarding these requirements is detailed below:
Transcripts: from all colleges and universities attended.
GRE General Test: Please note that the GRE General Test is optional for all graduate programs in the Department of Mathematics & Statistics for Fall 2024. If you have taken the GRE General Test and would like the Admissions Committee to consider your scores, you may submit them. However, your application will not be at a disadvantage if you do not submit scores.
English Proficiency: All applicants are required to demonstrate English proficiency, regardless of citizenship, unless they have completed a bachelor’s degree from an institution in the United States, Canada (excluding Quebec), the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, or New Zealand. See the GRS Application Guidelines for acceptable methods of demonstrating English proficiency.
Statement of Purpose: Required.
Resumé/CV: Required.
Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation are required.
Description: The Master of Science in Statistical Practice (MSSP) program is designed to provide students with the statistical skills necessary for success in business, government, and not-for-profit organizations. The program focuses on the effective application of statistical methods to the acquisition and analysis of data. It also emphasizes communication skills for conveying statistical ideas, models, and results to non-statistical audiences. Graduates are prepared for careers as practicing statisticians in industries such as finance, marketing, pharmaceutical, information technology, and government.
ScholarshipPercentage: 25% of tuition for first two semesters, potential additional 25% for summer

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Statistics
Requirements: Required Application Materials: Complete and submit the GRS online application. Official transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Three letters of recommendation are required. A statement of purpose is required. Please discuss why you are applying to the Master of Arts in Statistics at Boston University. Your statement should describe your academic background, research experience (if any), and future career goals. The GRE General Test is required. There is no minimum score required for admission. Our institution code is 3087. For more information, please visit the GRE website. TOEFL/IELTS (International Applicants Only): Required if you are not a US citizen or permanent resident, and your native language is not English, and you did not graduate from an undergraduate institution in the US or Canada. A minimum score of 90 on the TOEFL internet-based test (with minimum scores of 20 in each section), or a minimum score of 7.0 on the IELTS (with minimum scores of 6.5 in each section) is required. A current resume or curriculum vitae is required. The non-refundable application fee is $85.00.
Description: The MA in Statistics program provides advanced training in statistical methods and theory, along with important computational skills. The program is designed for students with strong quantitative backgrounds who wish to acquire a sophisticated understanding of statistics in preparation for either a career as a practicing statistician or for further graduate study in statistics or a related field. Students will learn how to apply powerful statistical methods to solve real-world problems. The program emphasizes the modern approach to statistics, which is data driven and heavily reliant on computation. The MA program provides a solid foundation in the theory and application of statistics and prepares students to analyze data in a wide range of fields, including bioinformatics, economics, education, engineering, environmental science, finance, public health, and social sciences. Full-time students complete the MA program in one academic year (two semesters). Part-time students may complete the program in two years.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based aid, Federal financial aid, Assistantships, Fellowships, Scholarships

ProgramName: PhD in Statistics
Requirements: All applicants must apply through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) online application system. The online application requires submission of: Transcripts from all prior undergraduate and graduate institutions. Three letters of recommendation. A personal statement. A resume or curriculum vitae. GRE General Test scores (subject tests not required). Non-native English speakers must submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. A non-refundable application fee.
Description: The PhD in Statistics program at Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts & Sciences provides students with a strong foundation in both classical and modern statistical theory and methodology, as well as computational statistics, statistical machine learning, and data science. The program trains students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they will conduct novel theoretical and methodological research, develop new statistical methods, and apply statistical principles to real-world problems. We welcome applicants with a strong background in mathematics and an interest in probability and statistics. Our program emphasizes flexibility, allowing students to tailor their coursework and research to their specific interests and career goals. Students work closely with faculty mentors on cutting-edge research projects, gaining hands-on experience in data analysis, statistical modeling, and scientific communication. As a student in the PhD in Statistics program, you will: Develop a deep understanding of statistical theory and methodology. Gain expertise in computational statistics and data science. Learn to conduct independent research and contribute to the field of statistics. Collaborate with faculty on innovative research projects. Prepare for a successful career in academia, industry, or government.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (tuition and health insurance scholarship), Service-based (stipend via Teaching/Research Assistantship)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry
Requirements: Applications for the MA and PhD programs in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry are submitted via the GRS online application. All application materials, including official transcripts, recommendations, and test scores, must be submitted through the online application. Three letters of recommendation are required. These letters should be written by faculty members who are familiar with your academic performance and potential for success in a graduate program. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended are required. Applicants should upload unofficial copies of their transcripts into the online application. Official transcripts will be required if admitted and matriculated. A Statement of Purpose is required. This statement should describe your research interests, academic background, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study at Boston University. It should be approximately 1-2 pages in length. A resume or curriculum vitae (CV) is required. It should include your educational background, research experience, publications (if any), presentations, honors, awards, and any relevant work experience. The GRE General Test is not required for applicants to the MA or PhD programs in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry. A writing sample is not required. International applicants must also demonstrate English proficiency through TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo.
Description: The Department of Biology offers an MA program in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry. This program provides students with advanced training in these fields through coursework and participation in a research laboratory. The program is specifically designed to prepare students for a career in biotechnology or for further graduate study toward a PhD. The department houses research groups with interests in molecular genetics, structural biology, membrane biophysics, bacterial physiology, cellular neurobiology, signal transduction, tumor biology, immunology, virology, and developmental biology. These laboratories employ a wide range of state-of-the-art methodologies. Students have the opportunity to select an area of research that matches their interests. All students participate in the weekly seminar series and several journal clubs. Students also acquire teaching experience by serving as teaching fellows in a laboratory course.

ProgramName: PhD in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry
Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges you have attended. Three letters of recommendation from faculty or research supervisors who are familiar with your academic and research abilities. A statement of purpose describing your motivation for pursuing a PhD, your research interests, and your future career goals. Please also include why you believe the BU MCBB program is a good fit for you. A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume outlining your academic background, research experience, publications, presentations, and any relevant work experience. International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through either the TOEFL or IELTS exam. This requirement may be waived under specific circumstances.
Description: The Department of Biology, Department of Chemistry, and Department of Medical Sciences & Education offer an interdisciplinary PhD in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology & Biochemistry. Students choose to specialize in one of these three participating departments or may pursue a truly interdisciplinary research program involving two or more of the participating departments. Students are prepared for careers in academia, biotechnology, and other scientific fields.
ScholarshipType: Full tuition scholarship, living stipend, health insurance contribution, in exchange for teaching or research assistantship services.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Musicology
Requirements: Applicants to the MA in Musicology must meet the admissions requirements of the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. In addition, applicants must submit the following materials directly to the School of Music, through the College of Fine Arts (CFA) Admissions website: A personal statement that describes academic background and interests, professional goals, and reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study at Boston University (300–500 words); A critical writing sample, such as a research paper from a previous course, that demonstrates analytical ability and facility with scholarly prose (15–25 pages); A curriculum vitae or resume; Letters of recommendation from three individuals who can speak to academic and professional qualifications; Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; GRE General Test scores are encouraged but not required; TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores (for international students only); Application fee.
Description: The MA in Musicology program is intended both for students who wish to pursue a doctorate in musicology or in an allied field, and for those who wish to enhance their professional capabilities (e.g., in teaching, librarianship, arts administration, or other careers for which advanced training in the critical and historical study of music is an asset). The program cultivates advanced skills in writing, critical thinking, research, and analysis of topics in musicology. Students take courses in musicological methods, bibliography, and a broad range of subjects in music history. The MA in Musicology program is part of the Department of Musicology & Ethnomusicology within the School of Music, College of Fine Arts. Visit the department website for more information.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (GRS Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Tuition Scholarships, Stipends)

ProgramName: PhD in Musicology
Requirements: All students must apply through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) online application. Review the GRS application information and instructions carefully before beginning your application. Complete applications must include: Transcripts, Three Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Curriculum Vitae (CV) / Résumé, Writing Samples, GRE General Test Scores (optional for applicants to the Musicology PhD and Ethnomusicology PhD for Fall 2024 admissions cycle and beyond; see below for additional detail), TOEFL/IELTS/PTE scores (for international applicants), Application Fee.
Description: Boston University offers PhDs in ethnomusicology, musicology, and music theory and composition. With small, intimate programs, students receive extensive individual attention and benefit from a wide variety of coursework within the School of Music, the Department of Musicology and Ethnomusicology, and the broader university. Doctoral students are fully funded for five years with tuition, health insurance, and a stipend. Many of our students teach in the undergraduate core curriculum, receive teaching certificates from BU’s Center for Teaching & Learning, and go on to tenure-track jobs. The PhD in Musicology at BU is designed to train independent scholars for careers in teaching and research, and to provide comprehensive grounding in all areas of historical musicology. Graduates have gone on to prestigious positions in academia and related fields.
MinimumGreScore: 80th percentile and above for the Verbal section, 70th percentile and above for the Quantitative section, 4.5 or higher for Analytical Writing
ScholarshipType: University Fellowship / Full Funding (includes full tuition waiver and stipend)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Neuroscience
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) in Neuroscience program is designed for students who desire a deeper understanding of the field and wish to enhance their academic credentials. The MA in Neuroscience can serve as a stepping stone for students interested in pursuing a PhD, or those who wish to build a strong foundation for a career in research or health-related professions. The MA program provides a broad foundation in neuroscience through core coursework and mentored research experiences in the laboratories of faculty who are members of the Graduate Program for Neuroscience (GPN). Students complete either a thesis (Plan A) or a non-thesis (Plan B) option depending on their interests and goals, with the thesis option providing more intensive research experience. Both plans require a minimum of 32 graduate credits.
ScholarshipAmount: Up to full tuition and a stipend
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, GRS Scholarships, Tuition Remission, Merit-based

ProgramName: PhD in Neuroscience
Requirements: The Graduate Program for Neuroscience (GPN) participates in the Boston University Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS) common application. Applications are submitted online through the GRS website. Please ensure you select “Neuroscience (PhD)” as your program of interest. All materials must be received by December 1 for fall admission of the following year. We do not accept spring admissions. Applications submitted by this deadline will be considered for admission and for Graduate School Fellowships. Please review the GRS Admissions page for additional details. Your Statement of Purpose (no more than two pages double-spaced) is a critical component of your application. This statement should explain your motivation for pursuing a PhD in Neuroscience, discuss any previous research experience you have, and describe your short-term and long-term career goals. Three letters of recommendation are required. These letters should be written by individuals who know you well and can comment on your academic abilities, research experience, and potential for success in a PhD program. They should be submitted directly by the letter writers through the online application system. You will be asked to upload transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended. Official transcripts will be required if you are admitted and choose to matriculate. The GRE General Test is not required for admission to the GPN. If you choose to submit GRE scores, they will be considered as part of your application. Scores should be sent directly to Boston University (GRE Institution Code: 3087). International students whose native language is not English and who have not received a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, or Australia must submit official scores from the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS). Scores should be no more than two years old. Minimum score requirements are: TOEFL iBT: 90 (with minimum scores of 20 in each section), IELTS: 7.0 (with minimum scores of 6.5 in each section). A non-refundable application fee is required at the time of application submission. Fee waivers may be available for eligible applicants. A curriculum vitae (CV) is required.
Description: The Graduate Program for Neuroscience (GPN) is an interdisciplinary PhD program based at the Boston University Charles River and Medical Campuses. Students in the GPN benefit from the breadth of neuroscience expertise across Boston University as they train in the field with faculty from multiple departments. Faculty research interests span the full spectrum of neuroscience, from molecules to mind and from discovery to clinical application. Students in the GPN are exposed to diverse research opportunities, a flexible curriculum, and numerous chances for professional development that prepare them for a variety of careers in neuroscience. Students completing the program are equipped to pursue careers in academia, industry, and related fields.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Global Policy
Requirements: Official Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation (3 required), Statement of Purpose, GRE Scores (optional), English Proficiency (for international students), Application Fee.
Description: Boston University’s Master of Arts in Global Policy (MAGP) program, offered jointly by the Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies and the Department of Political Science, addresses the growing demand for professionals who can understand and critically engage with complex global challenges. The program aims to educate students to become leaders who can apply theory to policy in an interdisciplinary way. Graduates will be equipped with critical thinking, analytical, and professional skills required to address global challenges in areas such as international security, international development, human rights, and diplomacy. Through a rigorous curriculum and practical experience, students will gain expertise in policymaking, policy analysis, and program evaluation within an international context. This program provides students with a strong foundation in global policy and prepares them for careers in international organizations, government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Affairs
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants for the MA in International Affairs should consult the GRS Admissions page for general requirements for all GRS degrees, as well as the International Relations page for requirements specific to International Relations degrees. The online application form and all supporting materials must be received by the application deadline.
Concentration: Diplomacy, Global Economic Affairs, Religion and International Affairs
Description: The MA in International Affairs is the Pardee School of Global Studies’ flagship graduate program, designed for students interested in careers in international service and global affairs. Our program is distinctive for combining the interdisciplinary study of global issues with professional training in policymaking. Our curriculum offers students the opportunity to learn from the Pardee School’s diverse faculty of scholars and practitioners. The program’s core curriculum emphasizes the study of analytical tools and frameworks for understanding international affairs. It also offers students the opportunity to develop and hone a wide range of analytical skills, including quantitative, qualitative, and historical methods. The Pardee School of Global Studies has a strong commitment to practical application and professional training. We provide numerous opportunities for students to apply their knowledge and skills in real-world settings through internships, practicums, and research projects. Our program prepares students for careers in government, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, and the private sector. Pardee School students are uniquely poised to address the most pressing global challenges of the 21st century. The MA program provides graduates with the analytical tools, professional skills, and global experience necessary to tackle these challenges effectively.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Graduate Teaching Fellowships, Graduate Research Assistantships, Dean's Scholarships, GRS Research Fellowships

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Relations / Master of Business Administration
Requirements:
Application Requirements
All applicants must apply online through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences online application.
Candidates for the MA in International Relations/MBA joint degree are evaluated on the basis of their academic records, recommendations, and relevant work, volunteer, or internship experience.
All applicants to the MA in International Relations/MBA program must submit the following:
*   Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
*   Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores OR Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) scores. Please note: Candidates may apply with the official results of either the GRE or the GMAT. Official GRE or GMAT scores must be sent directly from the Educational Testing Service (ETS) or Graduate Management Admission Council (GMAC) to Boston University. The GRE institution code for Boston University is 3087; the GMAT school code is X5X-55-90.
*   Three letters of recommendation.
*   A current CV or résumé.
*   A statement of purpose or personal statement (approximately 500 words).
*   For international students: Official English proficiency examination scores (TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE).
Department: Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies and Questrom School of Business
Description: The MA/MBA combined degree program at Boston University offers students the opportunity to combine a Master of Arts in International Relations with a Master of Business Administration. Offered jointly by the Pardee School of Global Studies and the Questrom School of Business, this program offers students an interdisciplinary education at the intersection of international affairs and management. Designed to be completed in two years, the MA/MBA program prepares students for careers in the private, public, and nonprofit sectors, working with multinational corporations, international financial institutions, or international organizations.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Relations / Juris Doctor
Requirements: Applicants apply to both schools concurrently and must meet the admissions criteria of both the School of Law and the Pardee School of Global Studies. This involves submitting applications separately to the School of Law (through LSAC) and to the Pardee School of Global Studies (via their online form), each with an application fee. Required documents include a Personal Statement/Statement of Purpose, Resume/Curriculum Vitae, Official Transcripts (submitted via LSAC CAS for Law), and Letters of Recommendation (CAS Report required for Law, two letters for Pardee). An LSAT score is required for the JD application. GRE scores are not required for MA admissions for Fall 2024 and beyond. English proficiency is also required for Pardee if applicable. Applicants may include an optional writing sample for both applications.
Department: School of Law and Pardee School of Global Studies
Fees: Year 1-3: $72,204/Year (School of Law); Year 4: $68,484/Year (Pardee School of Global Studies) (2024-2025 rates)
Fees.1: Year 1-3: $72,204/Year (School of Law); Year 4: $68,484/Year (Pardee School of Global Studies) (2024-2025 rates)
Description: The JD/MA in International Relations offers students the opportunity to combine the study of law with the study of international relations. Both degrees emphasize a critical and interdisciplinary approach to their subject matter. Students pursuing the dual degree receive training in legal analysis and the conceptual tools to understand global political, economic, and security relations, and prepare for careers in international organizations, government, non-governmental organizations, and global enterprises. The dual degree is designed to enable students to complete both degrees in four years rather than the five years typically required to complete each program separately. Students must apply for admission to the School of Law and to the Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies separately. Each school makes an independent decision on admission to its program, based on its own criteria. Students may apply to both programs simultaneously, or may apply to the Pardee School during their first year of study at the School of Law. Students enrolled in the JD/MA program must complete the full 85 credits required for the JD, and 32 of the 48 credits required for the MA in International Relations.
CostPerCredit: Varies. Year 1-3: Flat tuition. Year 4 (Pardee School): $2,138/credit (2024-2025 rates)
ScholarshipAmount: Varies. BU Law offers merit and need-based scholarships. Pardee School offers merit scholarships covering 25-75% of tuition.
ScholarshipPercentage: Nearly 90% of JD students receive financial aid. Pardee School merit scholarships average 50% of tuition for recipients.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Relations/International Affairs
Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities attended, three letters of recommendation, a personal statement, a writing sample (8-10 pages), a resume or curriculum vitae, official GRE General Test scores (optional for Fall 2024 admissions cycle and beyond), English proficiency examination, if applicable (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test), and application fee.
Department: Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies
Concentration: Diplomacy and International Cooperation, Development and Human Security, Global Economic Affairs, International Security, Religion and International Affairs, Individualized Specialization
Description: The Master of Arts (MA) program in International Relations at Boston University’s Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies is designed to prepare students for careers in foreign service, international organizations, non-governmental organizations, and global business. Our program offers a rigorous academic foundation combined with practical skills development, enabling graduates to address complex global challenges effectively. Students gain a deep understanding of international politics, economics, and security, while also developing expertise in specific regional or thematic areas. The MA in IR is a full-time, two-year program (4 semesters, 40 credits) that combines theoretical coursework with opportunities for research, internships, and professional development. Our faculty members are leading scholars and practitioners in the field, providing students with unparalleled mentorship and access to cutting-edge research.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in International Relations—Mid-Career Program
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the MA in International Relations—Mid-Career Program, applicants must submit: an online application, a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended, GRE scores (optional), English proficiency testing (if applicable), and a resume or curriculum vitae (CV). An academic writing sample is optional.
Description: The Mid-Career MA in International Relations is designed to provide rising leaders with the analytical tools and knowledge base necessary to tackle global challenges and succeed in an international career. This unique 16-month program allows professionals with substantial experience in a global field to expand their understanding of international affairs, sharpen their analytical skills, and develop their professional network. Students can tailor their academic experience to their interests, and the program encourages flexibility to pursue individualized interests in international relations.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Philosophy
Requirements: A complete application for the Master of Arts in Philosophy program at Boston University includes the online application for admission, application fee, transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended, three letters of recommendation, a personal statement, and an academic writing sample. GRE scores are optional for applicants to the MA program. English Proficiency Exam Scores are required if applicable.

ProgramName: PhD in Philosophy
Requirements: All PhD applicants must apply directly through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) online application system. Before beginning your application, please review the requirements listed below and the information for international applicants, if applicable. Once you begin your application, you can save your work and return to it later. All supplemental materials should be uploaded directly to the application. A complete application includes: Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume, Statement of Purpose, Writing Sample (for PhD applicants in the Humanities, Social Sciences, and Fine Arts only), Three Letters of Recommendation, Official Transcripts, English Proficiency (international applicants only), GRE General Test (required for some programs, see below), Application Fee. For a list of programs not requiring the GRE General Test, please visit this page.
Description: The Marquette University Philosophy Department offers a doctoral program in Philosophy. It is a traditional program, oriented toward the history of philosophy and continental European philosophy. The program offers a broad education in the history of Western philosophy from its beginnings to the present, while giving students the opportunity for more focused work in particular areas. The program prepares students for careers as teachers and scholars in philosophy. The program is committed to cultivating an appreciation for the historical and textual complexity of philosophical thought, training students to read and engage philosophical texts closely, and preparing students to take up the challenges of contemporary philosophical research and teaching. The PhD Program aims to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of the history of philosophy, while at the same time cultivating in students the ability to engage with the challenges of contemporary philosophical research. The program prepares students for academic careers in philosophy by training them to become effective teachers and scholars in their chosen fields of specialization.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Physics
Requirements: Thank you for your interest in the MA in Physics program! The MA program provides students with a solid foundation in the core areas of experimental and theoretical physics, while allowing them to specialize in areas of interest to them. This program is suitable for students interested in developing their physics background for further professional pursuits, teaching, or transitioning to other fields. We also have a PhD program in Physics. Applications are submitted through the GRS online application system. Please review the GRS Application Instructions carefully before applying.
Description: The Master of Arts in Physics offers students a broad introduction to advanced physics. The curriculum requires 32 credits beyond the bachelor’s degree, normally completed in one year. The program requires no thesis, but students may undertake research projects with faculty members for course credit. Students are encouraged to attend departmental seminars. Many MA students use the program as a stepping stone to doctoral study; others pursue teaching careers or employment in industry, government, and the private sector.

ProgramName: PhD in Physics
Requirements: Application Form, Application Fee, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation: At least two letters of recommendation are required, and three are preferred. Personal Statement, Resume or Curriculum Vitae, GRE Scores: Please check the department website to confirm whether GRE General Test and/or GRE Subject Test scores are required, optional, or not considered for your program. GRS requires official scores for any required GRE tests. English Proficiency: All applicants are required to demonstrate English proficiency, regardless of citizenship, if their first language is not English. Applicants to the PhD program in Physics should have a bachelor’s degree in physics or a closely related field. Exceptional students with a bachelor’s degree in physics, mathematics, or engineering are eligible to apply directly to the PhD program.
