Students admitted to the PhD program typically have a strong undergraduate record, including significant research experience, and a high level of performance on the physics GRE.
Description: The GRS PhD in Physics prepares students for careers in research and teaching through advanced coursework and in-depth research experience. Students typically complete required coursework during their first two years, including qualifying exams, and then dedicate the remainder of their time to original research for their dissertation. Areas of study include astronomy, astrophysics, condensed matter physics, biological physics, medical physics, elementary particle physics, and quantum information science, among others. Students benefit from close interactions with faculty, and from diverse research opportunities, including participation in the Boston University Photonics Center, which has state-of-the-art facilities for a wide range of interdisciplinary research, and membership in the BU Center for Space Physics. Graduates go on to pursue careers in academia, industry, and government, at institutions such as MIT, Harvard, Philips, Google, Los Alamos National Lab, CERN, and Raytheon.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Playwriting
Requirements: To apply for the Master of Fine Arts in Playwriting, please follow the instructions found on the GRS Admissions page. The required application materials for the Playwriting MFA include: Application form, Application fee, Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate work, Letters of Recommendation (3), Personal Statement/Statement of Purpose, CV/Resume, Writing Samples (see below), Proof of English proficiency (if applicable).
Department: College of Fine Arts, School of Theatre and College of Arts & Sciences, Department of English
Description: Boston University’s MFA in Playwriting program is an intensive, two-year experience designed to challenge and support playwrights as they develop their unique artistic voices. We believe that good playwrights need a thorough understanding of theatre history, dramatic literature, and current trends in professional theatre. Our students immerse themselves in new play development while taking courses in dramatic literature, playwriting, and theatre studies. They emerge with a comprehensive understanding of the craft of playwriting, a portfolio of new plays, and the skills needed to pursue professional careers. Students take courses alongside candidates for the MFA in Theatre Directing and the MA in Theatre Studies, as well as undergraduates, to create a lively and diverse community of theatre artists. Playwriting students are given multiple opportunities to develop and share their work with Boston University students and faculty, including student-directed workshops, readings, and thesis productions. The city of Boston is a vibrant arts community that offers students many opportunities to experience professional theatre. The BU School of Theatre is committed to providing students with the skills and experiences they need to succeed in the field.
Accredidation: Accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: Boston University’s Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) receives hundreds of applications annually from around the world. We seek candidates who demonstrate excellent academic preparation, intellectual curiosity, creativity, and the potential to succeed as graduate students and future professionals in their fields. A complete application to a GRS program includes the following items: Online Application, Transcripts, Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Resume/CV, and English Proficiency (if applicable). The GRE General Test is not required for admission to GRS master’s and PhD programs. A writing sample is required for the Political Science MA program.
Description: The MA in Political Science is a one-year program designed for students wishing to pursue further graduate study, or for those interested in a career in government or non-governmental organizations. The program’s rigorous curriculum provides students with a broad and deep understanding of political science as a discipline, with opportunities to specialize in a subfield, gain research experience, and deepen their methodological toolkit. Students completing the MA in Political Science program will possess the methodological training and substantive knowledge to successfully embark upon a career or doctoral studies. Most students complete the program in two semesters, though a three-semester option is available. The department awards several scholarships to MA students each year. See the Financial Aid section of the website for more information.

ProgramName: PhD in Political Science
Requirements: The application for admission to the PhD program in Political Science is completed through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. All applicants must submit the following materials: Official Transcripts for all undergraduate and graduate work; CV or Resume; Statement of Purpose; Three Letters of Recommendation; Writing Sample; GRE General Test Scores (Optional for 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 application cycles); International Applicants must also submit English Proficiency scores unless exempted.
Description: The Department of Political Science at Boston University offers a PhD program designed to train students for careers in teaching and research at major colleges and universities, and for positions in government and policy analysis. The program offers intensive training in four areas of study: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory. The program is committed to developing outstanding teachers and researchers through extensive coursework, independent research, and professional development training. Students completing the program are prepared to teach broadly in their chosen subfield(s), and to pursue an original research agenda that contributes to the discipline.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Psychology
Requirements: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions you have attended, three letters of recommendation, GRE General Test (optional for Fall 2024 admissions), Statement of Purpose, a resume or CV, application fee, and English proficiency (for international students).
Description: The MA program in Psychology is intended for students who wish to advance their general knowledge in experimental psychology, including areas such as cognitive, developmental, clinical, social, and neuroscience. Most students in the MA program plan to pursue a PhD in Psychology and use their MA year to gain research experience and prepare for doctoral studies. However, some MA students pursue career goals in areas such as market research, data analysis, public policy, or education. With a thesis option available, students can develop advanced research skills, which can serve as a strong foundation for future academic or professional pursuits.

ProgramName: PhD in Psychology
Requirements: All applications to the PhD program in Psychology must be submitted through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Application requirements detailed on the GRS Admissions page include: Application Form, Application Fee, Transcripts from all colleges and universities where a degree was received or courses were taken for credit toward a degree, Three Letters of Recommendation, and a Statement of Purpose (500-750 words). English Language Proficiency test scores (TOEFL/IELTS/PTE) are required for international students. GRE scores are NOT required for the Psychology PhD program.
Description: The PhD in Psychology is designed for students interested in careers in teaching and research in psychology. Our doctoral program trains students to become research scholars and prepares them for positions as faculty members at colleges and universities or as research scientists in government or private settings. The program offers specializations in Brain, Behavior & Cognition (BBC) and Clinical Psychology. Students work closely with faculty mentors, conducting original research and gaining teaching experience.
Accredidation: The Clinical Psychology Program is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA).

ProgramName: PhD in Religion
Requirements: Completed Application Form, Application Fee, Official Transcripts, Three Letters of Recommendation, A résumé or curriculum vitae (CV), Statement of Purpose, GRE General Test, TOEFL/IELTS (International students only), Writing Sample (for certain programs)
Concentration: Biblical Studies, Christianity & Culture, Ethics, History of Religions, Philosophy of Religion, Religion & Science, Sociology of Religion, Theology
Description: The PhD in Religion program prepares students for careers as scholars and teachers in colleges, universities, and seminaries. Our program, which emphasizes the critical study of religion as an academic discipline, is characterized by its interdisciplinary approach. It draws on the faculty expertise within the Graduate Program in Religion (GPR) and across the University, including the School of Theology. The GPR maintains a strong commitment to the intellectual study of religion, both in terms of theory and method, and in the critical analysis of diverse religious traditions and contexts. The program provides doctoral candidates with rigorous training in the academic study of religion while fostering intellectual curiosity, scholarly depth, and professional development.
ScholarshipType: Teaching fellowships, Research assistantships, Tuition scholarships (merit-based)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Religious Studies
Requirements: Applicants to the MA program should consult the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. In addition to these general requirements, applicants to the MA program in Religious Studies should submit: A statement of purpose (1,000–1,500 words) describing the applicant’s academic interests and goals, prior experience, and reasons for applying to the MA program in Religious Studies at Boston University. The statement should articulate the specific area(s) of religious studies that the applicant wishes to pursue. It should also identify the faculty in the department with whom the applicant would like to work and explain how their research interests align with those of the applicant. A writing sample (10–25 pages) from a prior academic course or publication. The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to conduct independent research, organize a sustained argument, and analyze texts clearly and incisively. Three letters of recommendation. Official Transcripts.
Description:
The Department of Religion offers a rigorous MA program in Religious Studies that can be completed in two or three semesters. Our MA students work closely with faculty in areas of their interest. Some pursue the MA as a freestanding degree for personal enrichment or professional development. Many regard the MA as a stepping stone to doctoral work. They find that our program prepares them well for pursuing a PhD in Religion at BU or elsewhere, and faculty take pride in helping students discern the next step in their careers and in preparing them for successful applications to doctoral programs. The MA is particularly strong for those who want to apply to BU’s PhD program, providing an ideal opportunity for students and faculty to get to know each other. Successful completion of the MA with a strong performance is often a good indicator for success in the PhD program.

All MA students choose a field of study and coursework that reflects their particular interests. Fields of study currently represented in our program include ancient Mediterranean religions, global Christianities, Islam, Judaism, theory and method, religion and science, religion and critical theory, religion and philosophy, and religion and literature. Courses are offered across these fields, and students are able to pursue their interests in their coursework and MA thesis.

MA students are also encouraged to participate in the intellectual life of the department by attending talks and lectures, participating in reading groups, and presenting their work. They contribute in important ways to the vibrancy of our community.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in French
Requirements: Applicants for the MA and PhD in French Studies apply through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Application Requirements for All Applicants: A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing the applicant’s academic and professional background, and indicating their reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in French at Boston University. Applicants should address their particular interests in French and Francophone studies, as well as their intellectual goals and career aspirations. Three letters of recommendation. Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. A writing sample (see below). Official GRE scores: GRE scores are waived for students applying for Fall 2024 admissions. Additional Requirements for International Applicants: Applicants whose native language is not English, and who have not received a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an institution in the United States, Canada (except Quebec), the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, or New Zealand, are required to submit official scores from the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test. Writing Sample: The writing sample should be 15-20 pages in length (double-spaced) in French or English. The sample should represent the applicant’s best critical or scholarly work.
Description: The MA in French provides students with a solid foundation in French and Francophone literatures, cultures, and critical theories. The program offers a balanced combination of breadth of coverage and opportunities for focused study, allowing students to develop expertise in areas of particular interest to them while also acquiring a comprehensive understanding of the field. Students benefit from close mentoring by a distinguished faculty, as well as from the diverse intellectual and cultural resources of Boston University and the greater Boston area. The MA is designed for students seeking to deepen their knowledge of French and Francophone studies and prepare for further graduate work at the PhD level. It is also suitable for high school teachers wishing to enhance their professional qualifications. The program aims to foster critical thinking, advanced research skills, and a nuanced understanding of French and Francophone cultures in their historical and global contexts. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers in education, cultural institutions, international organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: PhD in French
Requirements: All Ph.D. applicants should submit a statement of intent, three letters of recommendation, and a writing sample. Applicants are also required to submit a copy of their academic transcript(s) and GRE General Test scores (note: GRE subject test scores are not required). International students must also submit TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo scores.
Description:
The PhD in French provides rigorous training in literary and cultural history, critical theory, and the craft of teaching. The program offers comprehensive preparation for research and teaching in all aspects of French and Francophone literatures and cultures. Students will gain expertise in textual analysis and close reading, develop a deep understanding of literary theory and its applications, acquire thorough knowledge of French and Francophone intellectual and cultural history, and learn effective pedagogical strategies appropriate for college-level language and literature courses.
Areas of study include literature of all periods, cultural studies, critical theory, linguistics, and second language acquisition.
Candidates for the PhD in French are expected to command a working knowledge of Latin and one other Romance language (Italian or Spanish), or German, in addition to French and English.
The PhD in French consists of 16 semester courses (64 credits), a qualifying examination, and a dissertation. The courses are divided between the Department of Romance Studies (10 courses/40 credits) and another department or program (6 courses/24 credits) approved by the Director of Graduate Studies in French. All PhD students are required to acquire expertise in literary and critical theory by completing one course in theory offered by the Department of Romance Studies. Students typically spend two to three years in coursework, during which they also fulfill foreign language requirements and prepare for the qualifying examinations. The qualifying examinations are divided into two parts, oral and written. After passing the qualifying examination, students are admitted to PhD candidacy and proceed to research and write the dissertation. Students are expected to complete all requirements for the degree within seven years of matriculation.
Candidates for the PhD in French are eligible for teaching assistantships for up to four years, which include a stipend, tuition remission for eight courses, and eligibility for the Boston University Student Health Insurance Plan. Teaching assistants generally teach two courses per semester: one French language course and one discussion section for a literature course in translation.
AverageScholarshipAmount: $32,000/Year (Stipend) + Full Tuition Scholarship + Health Insurance Contribution
ScholarshipType: Merit-based (Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, GRS PhD Fellowships)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in French Language & Literature
Requirements: Applicants must submit Official Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, three Letters of Recommendation, a Personal Statement (approximately 500-750 words), and a Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV). English Proficiency Exams are required for international students from non-English speaking countries. The Graduate School of Arts & Sciences no longer requires or accepts GRE General Test scores for applicants to its master’s and PhD programs; any scores submitted will not be considered. A writing sample is required for most PhD programs and some MA programs; applicants should check their specific program of interest for details.
Description: The MA in French Language & Literature focuses on French and Francophone culture as an object of study, exploring literature, critical theory, and the history of ideas from a variety of theoretical approaches. Students work closely with faculty, developing proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing in French, cultivating their analytical and research skills, and gaining a comprehensive understanding of the French and Francophone worlds. Graduates of the program are prepared for doctoral work in French and other related fields or for careers in teaching, international relations, journalism, and more. Our graduates frequently teach at the university level as lecturers and professors. Students who complete the MA in French Language & Literature will be able to: Demonstrate advanced knowledge of literary theory and criticism; Conduct independent research and write a research paper of publishable quality; Teach French language and culture effectively at the college level.

ProgramName: PhD in French Language & Literature
Requirements: A completed online application form. Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose. A writing sample (20–25 pages in French). A CV/Resumé. A nonrefundable application fee. English proficiency testing for international students (TOEFL/IELTS/PTE scores). The GRE General Test is not required for admission to the PhD program in French Language & Literature.
Description: The PhD program in French Language & Literature at Boston University offers an intensive course of study for students who wish to engage in advanced research and teaching in French and Francophone cultures. With access to the intellectual resources of a major research university in a vibrant urban setting, students receive a rigorous training in critical methodologies and cultural theories. With courses across all periods—medieval, early modern, eighteenth, nineteenth, twentieth, and twenty-first centuries—and across French, Francophone African, and Caribbean literatures and cultures, students gain a comprehensive understanding of the field. Students benefit from the close guidance of faculty in preparing for preliminary exams, writing their dissertations, and on the job market. Students are also given extensive training and experience in the teaching of French language and literature, leading to the opportunity to teach independently in their later years of study. Our PhD graduates have gone on to hold tenure-track and other academic positions at institutions such as the University of Massachusetts-Dartmouth, the University of Colorado-Boulder, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Kenyon College, Reed College, the University of Nevada-Reno, and the American University in Cairo, as well as positions in publishing and other fields.
ScholarshipType: Full Tuition Scholarship, Stipend, Health Insurance, Fellowships, Assistantships (Teaching or Research)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Spanish
Requirements: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Two letters of recommendation. Statement of purpose. Writing sample. TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE scores (for international applicants). Official GRE scores are not required for MA applicants.
Description: The MA in Hispanic Language & Literatures at Boston University’s Department of Romance Studies is designed to prepare students for doctoral study and careers in teaching. The program offers graduate-level training in Spanish literature, culture, and linguistics. It also affords students the opportunity to spend a semester in Madrid, Spain, where they can deepen their knowledge of Spanish culture and language while earning graduate credit.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Dean's Scholarships, Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Conference Travel Grants

ProgramName: PhD in Spanish
Requirements: For application to all graduate programs in Romance Studies, prospective students should submit the following through the Boston University Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) online application system: The online application form, Transcripts from all previous colleges and universities, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose (1–2 pages), An academic writing sample (in English or the target language, 10–20 pages). The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is NOT required for admission to our graduate programs. For international students, a TOEFL or IELTS score.
Description: The PhD in Spanish offers students the opportunity to undertake advanced work in the literatures and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world or in Hispanic linguistics. Our faculty’s diverse research interests span the linguistic and literary traditions of Spain, Spanish America, and the United States, from the medieval period to the present day. PhD candidates in Spanish may focus their studies in areas such as Peninsular literature, Latin American literature, or Hispanic linguistics. The program requires a minimum of 16 semester courses, or 64 credits, beyond the BA. Students are expected to demonstrate strong proficiency in Spanish as well as in a second foreign language. Graduate students frequently work with the editorial staff of the Journal of Hispanic Philology, which is housed in the Department of Romance Studies.
AverageScholarshipAmount: Full tuition remission and an annual living stipend (specific stipend amount not explicitly stated on BU website)
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition remission and an annual living stipend (specific stipend amount not explicitly stated on BU website)

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Hispanic Language & Literatures
Requirements: A complete application includes an Application Form, Application Fee, a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, and a writing sample of approximately 15 pages in length, preferably on a topic in Hispanic literature (the writing sample may be in English or Spanish). GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. For international students, a TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test score is required.
Description: The MA in Hispanic Language & Literatures provides students with a thorough grounding in Hispanic literary and cultural studies, as well as Hispanic linguistics. It also develops students’ critical and research skills. A hallmark of the MA program is its flexibility, allowing students to tailor their programs of study according to their individual interests and career goals. Students may pursue a general MA in Hispanic Language & Literatures, or they may choose to focus their studies in a particular area, such as a specific period, genre, or region; Latin American or Iberian studies; or Hispanic linguistics. The MA program can also serve as a useful credential for those applying to PhD programs in Hispanic Language & Literatures.
ScholarshipType: Department- or program-specific aid, outside scholarships, research assistantships (RAs), teaching assistantships (TAs)

ProgramName: PhD in Hispanic Language & Literatures
Requirements: The online application requires an Application Form, Application Fee, CV/Resume, Statement of Purpose (a two- to three-page essay outlining academic and professional qualifications, reasons for seeking a graduate degree, academic and research interests, fit with faculty, related experiences, and future goals), unofficial Transcripts from all institutions where you have received a degree (official transcripts required upon admission), Three Letters of Recommendation (submitted through the online application system), Writing sample (up to 20 pages in length), GRE General Test (optional for all PhD programs), and English Proficiency (for International Applicants).
Description:
Boston University’s PhD in Hispanic Language & Literatures offers doctoral training in Iberian, Latin American, and Latinx cultural production from the medieval period to the present. The program allows students to specialize in a variety of fields of study, including literature, film, visual culture, critical theory, and cultural studies.
Our students have the opportunity to participate in a dual degree program with the Universidad de Santiago de Compostela in Spain, through which they can obtain a PhD from both institutions.
Students work closely with faculty members on a diverse range of topics, including medieval and early modern peninsular literature and culture, transatlantic studies, colonial and postcolonial studies, film and visual culture, modern and contemporary Latin American and Peninsular literature, critical theory, gender studies, translation studies, Latinx studies, human rights, ecocriticism, and the medical humanities.
The Department of Romance Studies is also home to the Latin American Studies Program and the Latinx Studies Initiative, both of which offer regular programming and resources to our students. Our graduates have pursued careers in academia and in the nonprofit, public, and private sectors.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Sociology
Requirements: Required application materials include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, and a resume/CV. The GRE is not required for admission to the MA in Sociology program. No writing sample is required for the MA program.
Description: The MA in Sociology offers students broad training in sociological theory and methods, with opportunities for in-depth study in a variety of substantive areas. Students are trained to critically analyze and understand social life at micro and macro levels. With its strong emphasis on research and writing, the MA program is an excellent stepping stone for students interested in pursuing a PhD or a career in research, policy analysis, advocacy, public service, or private industry. The MA is a two-year, 8-course (32-credit) program.
ScholarshipType: Teaching Fellowships, Research Assistantships, Graduate Assistantships, GRS Tuition Scholarships, Dean's Fellowships

ProgramName: PhD in Sociology
Requirements: All applicants to the PhD program must apply through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Successful applicants generally have an outstanding record of academic achievement, including significant coursework in sociology or a related social science discipline (e.g., economics, political science, psychology, anthropology, public health). It is not necessary to have an MA degree prior to admission to the PhD program. Students admitted to the program generally receive full tuition scholarships and stipends. While a significant number of our students have prior Master's degrees, many enter our PhD program directly from an undergraduate institution. For more information, please visit the GRS Admissions page. All applicants must meet the general requirements of the GRS as well as the specific requirements of the Department of Sociology. Required documents include: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, Curriculum vitae (CV), Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Writing sample, Official GRE General Test scores are *not* required for admission. If you do submit GRE scores, they will be considered as part of your overall application. Official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores (international applicants only, unless exempt).
Description: The PhD Program in Sociology at Boston University is committed to training the next generation of scholars who will make original contributions to sociological theory, research methods, and substantive fields of inquiry. Our program takes pride in providing students with a deep knowledge of core sociological areas and advanced research skills, while fostering intellectual curiosity and creativity to pursue their own interests. Students are encouraged to pursue interdisciplinary work, take advantage of the diverse intellectual resources available at Boston University, and collaborate with faculty and fellow graduate students. Our graduates pursue careers in academia and other research-intensive fields.
AverageScholarshipAmount: $105,540/Year (includes full tuition scholarship, $38,500 9-month stipend, and health insurance fee)
ScholarshipAmount: $105,540/Year (includes full tuition scholarship, $38,500 9-month stipend, and health insurance fee)
ScholarshipType: Full-tuition scholarship, Stipend, Health Insurance Fee; Merit-based

ProgramName: PhD in Sociology & Social Work
Requirements: Applicants to the PhD program in Sociology & Social Work must submit all materials directly through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences online application. Application requirements include: Online Application Form, Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Three letters of recommendation, A 1,000–1,500 word statement of purpose describing your interest in the PhD program, your research interests, and your future career goals, A writing sample (e.g., term paper, master’s thesis chapter, or professional report) of no more than 30 pages, The GRE General Test is required, English language proficiency if you are an international applicant.
Department: Boston University School of Social Work and Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (Department of Sociology)
Description: Boston University’s PhD program in Sociology & Social Work is a joint doctoral program offered by the Department of Sociology in the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) and the School of Social Work (SSW). The program combines the scientific study of sociology with the professional application of social work in an integrated curriculum designed to produce a new generation of leaders for scholarship and teaching in social work and sociology. Graduates are prepared for careers in academic research, teaching, and policy analysis and evaluation across a range of settings.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Fellowships, Teaching Fellowships (TF), Research Assistantships (RA), Dean's Fellowships

ProgramName: Advanced Graduate Certificate in Biogeoscience
Requirements: Applicants should have a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in biology, earth sciences, environmental sciences, or a related field; basic knowledge of calculus, statistics, chemistry, and physics; and previous experience in field or laboratory research. Prior graduate-level coursework in these areas will strengthen an application. Applicants to the Advanced Graduate Certificate in Biogeoscience must submit the following materials: Online Application, Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions, Three letters of recommendation, A personal statement describing academic interests and career goals, Resume or CV, An official GRE score (general test) or waiver
Description:
Boston University’s Advanced Graduate Certificate in Biogeoscience provides graduate students with advanced interdisciplinary training in biogeoscience, leveraging expertise across departments and colleges. The certificate enhances students’ understanding of the interactions between physical, chemical, geological, and biological processes on Earth, and their sensitivity to both natural and anthropogenic environmental change. The certificate emphasizes the importance of quantitative approaches to address critical challenges in environmental change research and aims to foster a new generation of scientists who can bridge traditional disciplinary divides to tackle complex environmental problems facing society.
The Graduate Certificate in Biogeoscience is administered by the Department of Earth & Environment through the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. The certificate is offered to students currently enrolled in a master’s or doctoral program at Boston University who wish to broaden their interdisciplinary knowledge and skills.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in African Studies
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university and meet the general admission requirements of the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences. Required application materials include the online CAS Graduate Application, unofficial transcripts (official upon admission), two letters of recommendation, a personal statement/statement of purpose, and a resume/CV. The GRE General Exam is not required for this program. English proficiency is required for non-native English speakers.
Fees: $19,460 total (based on 20 credits at $973/credit for 2024-2025 academic year)
Fees.1: $19,460 total (based on 20 credits at $973/credit for 2024-2025 academic year)
Description: The Graduate Certificate in African Studies is designed for graduate students who wish to supplement their master’s or doctoral studies with a specialization in African Studies. The program is flexible and can be customized to suit individual needs and academic interests. We welcome students from all departments in the College of Arts and Sciences, as well as students from the Schools of Law, Medicine, Theology, and Education. Students in the graduate certificate program study the politics, cultures, and societies of Africa, drawing on a wide range of disciplines in the humanities and social sciences. Upon completion of the certificate, students will be able to demonstrate a broad, interdisciplinary knowledge of Africa; a deeper understanding of a particular region or topic within Africa; and proficiency in an African language.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Asian Studies
Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Three letters of recommendation. Official GRE General Test scores (if required by your program). Official English proficiency exam scores (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE) (international applicants only). A statement of purpose (approximately 1,000 words, unless otherwise specified by your program) outlining your academic interests and professional goals. A current resume or curriculum vitae. A writing sample (if required by your program).
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Asian Studies offers students a systematic understanding of the history, politics, societies, and cultures of Asia. Focusing on China, Japan, Korea, and South Asia, the Certificate provides students with the critical skills and knowledge needed to engage with the complex and dynamic issues facing the region. Designed for graduate students from any discipline, the program enhances their understanding of Asia and demonstrates their commitment to the study of the region. Through interdisciplinary coursework, language training, and research opportunities, students gain a comprehensive perspective on Asian affairs and prepare for careers in academia, government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in European Studies
Requirements: Applicants to the Graduate Certificate in European Studies must either be currently enrolled in a GRS master’s or doctoral program, or have completed an MA or PhD degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all institutions of higher education attended. A current resume or curriculum vitae. A statement of purpose (1–2 pages). Three letters of recommendation (not required for current BU graduate students).
Description: The Graduate Certificate in European Studies provides graduate students at Boston University the opportunity to specialize in the interdisciplinary field of European Studies. Students can pursue the certificate either in conjunction with a master’s or doctoral program or as a standalone certificate program. Students gain interdisciplinary knowledge of Europe through coursework in the humanities and social sciences. The certificate is especially valuable for students pursuing careers in academia, government, international relations, or non-profit organizations where an interdisciplinary understanding of Europe is an asset. Students have the opportunity to participate in the European Studies program’s many events, including the Monday lecture series, graduate student workshops, conferences, and career events. They also have access to dedicated advising and professional development support.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Holocaust, Genocide & Human Rights Studies
Requirements: Boston University students interested in pursuing the Graduate Certificate should submit an application to the Director of the Elie Wiesel Center for Jewish Studies by April 15 of their first year of graduate study. The application should include a letter of intent explaining how the certificate fits with their graduate studies and career goals, a current CV, and a current transcript.
Description: Boston University’s Graduate Certificate in Holocaust, Genocide & Human Rights Studies offers a rigorous interdisciplinary approach to the study of the Holocaust, mass violence, and human rights. This certificate is ideal for graduate students interested in pursuing advanced research and scholarship in the field as well as professionals working for non-governmental organizations and other institutions. Drawing on the expertise of faculty across several departments and schools, the Certificate provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the historical, sociological, political, cultural, and ethical dimensions of these phenomena. Students will engage with historical narratives, theoretical frameworks, and contemporary issues to develop critical analytical skills and a nuanced perspective on the causes, consequences, and prevention of genocide and human rights abuses.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Latin American Studies
Requirements: All applicants to the Latin American Studies Certificate, whether enrolled in a BU graduate degree program or applying as a stand-alone applicant, must submit the following: Online application form, Official transcripts from all universities and colleges previously attended, Two letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, A writing sample in English or Spanish, Current resume/CV
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Latin American Studies is available to students in PhD, MA, or MS programs at Boston University who wish to enrich their knowledge of Latin America. With the approval of their primary department, students may count up to two courses used for the certificate toward their other graduate degrees.

ProgramName: GRS Graduate Certificate in Linguistics
Requirements:
Applicants to the PhD, MA, and graduate certificate programs are not required to submit GRE scores.
Applicants to the Linguistics graduate programs (PhD, MA, Certificate) must submit the following materials directly to the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences through the GRS online application portal:
Statement of Purpose: A two-to-three page statement describing your academic background, your reasons for wishing to pursue graduate study in Linguistics at Boston University, and your long-term academic and professional goals.
Letters of Recommendation: Three letters of recommendation from faculty members or others qualified to assess your academic potential.
Writing Sample: A paper or substantial excerpt from a paper, preferably on a linguistic topic, demonstrating your ability to formulate and support an argument.
Official Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions.
Resume/CV
Application Fee
TOEFL/IELTS scores for international applicants (if applicable).
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Linguistics is designed for students enrolled in other Boston University graduate programs who seek to enhance their studies with a strong foundation in linguistics. The certificate allows students to explore core areas in linguistics and develop expertise in linguistic analysis and theory. The program also offers students the opportunity to apply linguistic principles and methods to interdisciplinary research questions within their primary field of study. The certificate also serves as an excellent foundation for PhD study in linguistics.

ProgramName: Certificate in Museum Studies
Description: The Museum Studies Certificate Program provides graduate students with a solid grounding in the theory and practice of museum work, preparing them for professional careers in museums and related organizations, or for further graduate study in museum studies. Students learn the fundamental concepts and practical skills necessary to work in museums and related cultural institutions, including curatorial practice, exhibition development, museum education, collections management, and museum administration. The program is flexible and interdisciplinary, allowing students to tailor their coursework to their particular interests and career goals. Students also gain valuable hands-on experience through internships at local, national, and international museums. The certificate complements a master’s or doctoral degree in a wide range of academic disciplines, including history, art history, archaeology, American studies, anthropology, and education.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Muslim Studies
Requirements: Applicants for GRS certificate programs must submit an application form, official transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. A Statement of Purpose is required. All applicants whose native language is not English are required to demonstrate English proficiency, regardless of citizenship status. Writing samples, resumes/CVs, and GRE scores are required for some programs; applicants should consult departmental requirements for specific details.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Muslim Studies offers students an opportunity to explore the historical and contemporary dimensions of Islam and Muslim societies. The program is specifically designed to provide students enrolled in doctoral programs at Boston University, as well as qualified students enrolled in other degree programs and those with an MA, with a firm grounding in the academic study of Muslim societies, especially in the humanities and social sciences. Drawing on a range of disciplinary methods, including history, anthropology, sociology, and religious studies, the certificate program covers a variety of topics, including Islamic law, theology, and philosophy; Sufism; gender and sexuality in Islam; contemporary Muslim political thought; Islam in America; and the arts and literatures of Muslim cultures. The certificate is especially valuable for students who wish to demonstrate an academic specialization in Muslim Studies, or who plan to conduct research and teach in the field. The program is administered by the Department of Religion.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Teaching Language, Literature & Film
Requirements: These certificates are open to Boston University graduate students currently enrolled in MA or PhD programs, and they offer an additional credential and specialized training in a particular field.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Teaching Language, Literature, & Film provides graduate students from departments across the university with the opportunity to refine and enhance their professional training in the theory and practice of teaching language, literature, and/or film. This certificate is open to all CAS graduate students—MA, MFA, and PhD—who are currently enrolled in a degree program at BU. The certificate can be earned concurrently with a graduate degree or after the degree has been conferred. Students are required to take 16 credits (4 courses) for this certificate.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Teaching Writing
Requirements: General Application Requirements for all CAS graduate programs (unless otherwise noted by your program of interest): Unofficial transcripts from all universities and colleges attended are required at the time of application. If admitted, official transcripts from all institutions where a degree was or will be conferred will be required at the time of matriculation. Two letters of recommendation are required. Statement of Purpose: Required for all applications. Please refer to your program’s website for specific essay prompts or length requirements. GRE Scores: Please refer to your program’s website for specific GRE requirements, if any. The GRE is not required for many programs within the GRS. Check the specific program’s website for more information. Writing Sample: Required for some programs. Please refer to your program’s website for specific requirements. Resume/CV: Required for some programs. Please refer to your program’s website for specific requirements. Application Fee: All applicants are required to pay a non-refundable application fee of $85. English Proficiency: All applicants whose native language is not English, and who did not receive their undergraduate degree from an institution where the language of instruction is English, are required to submit official scores from either the TOEFL or IELTS exam.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Teaching Writing is an academic credential for individuals interested in strengthening their expertise in teaching writing. The Certificate is appropriate for writing teachers in higher education settings, secondary school English and humanities teachers, and individuals in professions that require extensive writing and writing instruction. Upon completion of the Graduate Certificate in Teaching Writing, students will be able to: Articulate a rhetorical theory of writing and apply it to their teaching practices; Identify principles of effective writing instruction and implement them in their teaching; Design instruction that addresses individual student needs and diverse learning styles; Adapt their teaching for diverse learning environments and technological applications; Articulate a robust theory of the writing process and apply it to their teaching practices; Identify pedagogical principles of effective writing instruction and implement them in their teaching.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Women's, Gender, & Sexuality Studies
Requirements:
The Graduate Certificate in Women’s, Gender, & Sexuality Studies is only available to students already enrolled in a graduate program at Boston University or at its affiliated schools, or to students who have completed a graduate degree at Boston University or at its affiliated schools. If you are not currently enrolled in a BU graduate program, or have not completed a BU graduate degree, please refer to the GRS application page for instructions.
To apply for the Certificate, please submit the following:
*   A brief statement explaining your interest in the Certificate and how it will enhance your overall graduate training.
*   An unofficial transcript.
*   A letter from your current Director of Graduate Studies, or from your academic advisor, confirming that you are in good standing in your current graduate program. If you have already completed your graduate degree, please submit a letter from your former Director of Graduate Studies or academic advisor, confirming your good standing.
*   A completed application form.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Women’s, Gender, & Sexuality Studies (WGSS) offers students the opportunity to complement their graduate work in other fields with sustained training in the interdisciplinary field of WGSS. The certificate requires students to complete a total of 16 credits (4 courses) from an approved list of courses. The graduate certificate is administered by the Women’s, Gender, & Sexuality Studies Program and open to graduate students enrolled in other departments and schools at Boston University. Students will receive training in the theoretical and methodological approaches foundational to WGSS, as well as an introduction to current scholarship and research within the field. The WGSS Certificate enables students to deepen their understanding of how gender and sexuality shape our everyday lives, politics, and culture, and will provide them with an interdisciplinary perspective from which to pursue careers in a wide array of fields and/or continue their graduate work in WGSS. The certificate will appear on students’ official transcripts.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American & Black Diaspora Studies
Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application (BU-specific questions for either platform are included), Official High School Transcript(s), School Report & Counselor Recommendation, Two Teacher Evaluations, SAT/ACT Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 & 2025 First-Year Applicants), Proof of English Proficiency (for international students), Application Fee or Fee Waiver
Description: Boston University’s undergraduate program in African American & Black Diaspora Studies, housed in the College of Arts & Sciences, focuses on the history, culture, and politics of people of African descent throughout the world. The curriculum encourages students to explore how race and racialization have shaped institutions and social relations, both historically and in the contemporary moment. Students are provided with critical tools to study Black history, cultures, and societies in a global context, with particular attention to transnational connections among African peoples across the diaspora. Our multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach combines the rigor of humanities and social science disciplines to promote critical thinking, advanced research, and written and oral communication skills relevant to a diverse range of post-graduate pursuits. Majors in African American & Black Diaspora Studies are well prepared for careers in fields such as law, medicine, education, journalism, public policy, community organizing, and the arts, as well as for further graduate study across the humanities and social sciences.
ScholarshipAmount: From $20,000 to $25,000 per year, with some covering full tuition

ProgramName: Minor in African Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Minor in African Studies, please fill out the Declaration of Minor Form and bring it to the African Studies Center (232 Bay State Road, Room 402). A signed copy will be returned to you for your records. Once your form is signed, please email it to the Registrar’s office for processing.
Department: Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies
Description: Boston University’s Minor in African Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give undergraduates a broad knowledge of Africa and to allow them to focus on a particular discipline or area of interest. Students take a combination of required and elective courses from a range of disciplines offered by various departments and schools across the University, including courses on the history, politics, societies, cultures, religions, and arts of Africa, as well as several African languages. Students may also pursue study abroad in Africa, or participate in the African Studies Center’s internship program in Africa or the African diaspora. These experiences are highly recommended for the Minor in African Studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application, BU Questions, Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, School Report, Teacher Evaluation, Midyear Report (if applicable), Test Scores (SAT/ACT, optional for Fall 2024 and beyond), English Proficiency (if applicable), Financial Aid Application (if applicable)
Description: The American Studies major focuses on the United States and its place in the world, with particular attention to how ideas of America and American-ness have been produced, challenged, and transformed from the colonial period to the present. The program offers students an interdisciplinary approach to studying the United States, drawing on insights and methods from across the humanities and social sciences. Students are encouraged to develop their own critical perspectives on American culture, society, and history, and to cultivate the skills necessary to engage in public discourse about the past, present, and future of the nation. The American Studies program cultivates critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and effective communication—skills that are highly valued in a wide range of professions. Graduates pursue careers in fields such as law, journalism, public policy, education, museum studies, and nonprofit management. Many also go on to graduate school in history, literature, or other related disciplines.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application (including essays); Official High School Transcript(s); School Report and Counselor Recommendation; Two Teacher Evaluations; Mid-Year Report (if applicable).
Description: Boston University’s undergraduate major in Anthropology (BA) provides students with a broad and rigorous exposure to the core subfields of anthropology – sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, and biological anthropology – and an appreciation of their historical development, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Our curriculum emphasizes the dynamic interconnections among these subfields as they explore the range of human experience and behavior, past and present, in socio-cultural, biological, and archaeological contexts. Students are encouraged to develop a deeper understanding of anthropology through hands-on research opportunities and field programs both in Boston and abroad (e.g., our summer archaeological field school, field research in Ecuador, and other opportunities offered through the Boston University Study Abroad program). Beyond the classroom, our students have engaged in a wide range of internship opportunities at such places as the Peabody Essex Museum, the Museum of Fine Arts, the Boston Children’s Museum, local archaeological firms, and cultural organizations that serve Boston’s diverse immigrant communities. Anthropology majors also pursue diverse career paths after graduation, including medicine and public health, international relations, social justice and advocacy, museum work, and academia, among many others. The BA program in Anthropology thus provides students with the intellectual tools for understanding a complex and interconnected world and the skills that are increasingly valued by employers in a globalized society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Archaeology
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application or QuestBridge Application, along with Boston University Member Questions. Required documents include an Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, and Teacher Evaluation. A Midyear Grade Report and proof of English Proficiency (if applicable) are also necessary. Applicants must pay an Application Fee or qualify for a Fee Waiver. The application also requires a personal essay submitted through the Common Application and a short essay (250 words) in response to the prompt: "What about Boston University interests you?"
Description: Archaeology at Boston University is a distinct interdisciplinary program designed to give students a global and multicultural perspective on societies, both ancient and recent. Our faculty specializes in the archaeology of Europe, the Mediterranean, the Near East, Mesoamerica, and North America. Archaeology BA students master the foundational theories, methodologies, and ethics of archaeology, as well as the history, ecology, and social organization of past human societies. The BA program provides excellent preparation for further study in graduate school or for careers in related fields such as cultural resource management, museums, education, or historical preservation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies
Requirements:
Common Application or Coalition Application with the Boston University Questions
Official High School Transcript(s)
Counselor Recommendation
School Report
Two Teacher Evaluations
Midyear Grades (if available)
English Proficiency (if applicable)
Test-Optional Policy (see below)
Optional Arts Portfolio (only if applicable, see below)
Optional Alumni Interview
Application Fee or Fee Waiver
Description: Asian Studies at Boston University offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate major that addresses the histories, cultures, politics, and societies of Asia. Students gain critical insight into the diverse regions of East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) and South/Southeast Asia (India, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, etc.), and they develop expertise in at least one Asian language. The program emphasizes a holistic approach, encouraging students to explore Asia from multiple disciplinary perspectives, including history, political science, anthropology, religion, and literature. Graduates are prepared for careers in government, international relations, journalism, education, business, and further graduate study, equipped with strong analytical skills, cross-cultural competence, and deep knowledge of one of the world’s most dynamic and influential continents.
ScholarshipAmount: Trustee Scholarship: Full tuition; Presidential Scholarship: $25,000/year

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Astronomy
Requirements: To be considered for admission to Boston University, first-year applicants must submit the following materials: Common Application or Coalition Application; Boston University Questions (within the Common Application or Coalition Application, including a short essay related to our unique approach to education); Application Fee or Fee Waiver; Official High School Transcript; Counselor Recommendation and School Report; Teacher Evaluation; Standardized Test Scores (SAT or ACT) – see our test policy; English Proficiency (if applicable); Portfolio, Audition, or Interview (if applicable to your program).
Description: As an astronomy student in BU’s College of Arts & Sciences (CAS), you’ll explore the vast, evolving universe through a challenging curriculum of physics, mathematics, and astronomy courses. You’ll be encouraged to get involved in research with faculty in areas such as observational and theoretical astrophysics, planetary science, solar physics, and instrumentation. Astronomy majors develop strong quantitative and analytical skills that serve them well, not only in graduate school, but in a wide variety of careers including science education, science policy, data science, and scientific computing. A BA in Astronomy is a good choice for students interested in a broad liberal arts education, or those wishing to combine their study of astronomy with a second major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biology
Requirements:
Your application will include the following items:
Common Application or Coalition Application
We accept both the Common Application and the Coalition Application. The Common Application and Coalition Application both include an essay component. Please note that Boston University does not have a separate essay beyond what is required by the Common Application or Coalition Application.
BU Questions
Within the Common Application and Coalition Application, you will find Boston University’s specific questions. You can fill these out directly within the application.
Secondary School Report & Counselor Recommendation
Your high school counselor should submit a Secondary School Report, which includes a letter of recommendation. If you attend a school where a counselor is not assigned, the school principal or headmaster may complete this form.
Teacher Evaluation
One Teacher Evaluation is required. We recommend selecting a teacher who has taught you in a core academic subject (English, math, science, social studies, or a world language) within the last two years of your secondary school career.
Transcripts
Official transcripts from all secondary schools attended are required.
SAT or ACT Scores
Boston University requires applicants to submit official SAT or ACT scores. We will superscore both the SAT and ACT, using your highest scores from each section across all test dates. The SAT Essay and ACT Writing sections are not required.
English Proficiency
Applicants whose native language is not English and who have not attended an English-medium secondary school for at least three years are required to demonstrate English proficiency. Visit our International Students page for additional details.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Biology provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the biological sciences, a mastery of basic research skills, and an appreciation of the social and ethical aspects of biology. The BA program is designed for students who want a strong foundation in biology, but also wish to have the flexibility to pursue other academic interests, such as a second major or minor, or pre-professional studies outside of the sciences. The BA in Biology prepares students for careers in diverse fields such as medicine, dentistry, public health, law, business, education, and science writing. It also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in biology or related fields.
ScholarshipAmount: Trustee Scholarship (full tuition), Dean's Scholarship ($25,000 per year)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
Requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application: Complete and submit the Common Application or Coalition Application online. Your application must include the essay. Secondary School Report: This form is completed by your school counselor and must include your official high school transcript. Counselor Recommendation: Your school counselor must submit a letter of recommendation on your behalf. Teacher Evaluation: A letter of recommendation is required from one teacher (preferably in a core academic subject) who has taught you in an academic course. Official High School Transcript: As noted above, this should be included with your Secondary School Report. Standardized Test Scores: For students applying for Fall 2024 admission, SAT and ACT scores are optional. For information on submitting scores, please visit our Standardized Test Scores webpage. Please note that some scholarships may require test scores. English Proficiency: If English is not your first language, you must submit official scores from an English proficiency exam. Please visit our English Proficiency webpage for full details. Mid-Year Report: Submit your Mid-Year Report and updated high school transcript to BU Admissions when your first-term senior grades are available. The Mid-Year Report is found in the Common Application or Coalition Application.
ScholarshipAmount: Ranges from $20,000–$25,000 per year, up to full tuition

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit their application via either the Common Application or the Coalition Application. Required materials include: High School Transcript(s), Counselor Recommendation, School Profile, Teacher Recommendation, Mid-Year Grade Report, an $80 Application Fee or Fee Waiver, and English Proficiency Exam Results (if applicable).
Description: The Department of Chemistry offers two undergraduate degrees: a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Chemistry and a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Chemistry. Both degrees provide a strong background in the major areas of chemistry. The BS degree is more intensive, designed for students who are preparing for a career in chemistry or related fields, or for graduate study in chemistry. Students are encouraged to participate in research with faculty members in Chemistry, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, or other departments. Opportunities for research include during the academic year, the summer, and a semester in BU’s study abroad program in Dresden, Germany.
Accredidation: Certified by the American Chemical Society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cinema & Media Studies
Requirements: Applicants for first-year admission must submit the Common Application or QuestBridge Application, Boston University Questions, Essays (personal essay), Official High School Transcript(s), Secondary School Report & Counselor Recommendation, and Teacher Evaluation (from an academic teacher). SAT or ACT scores are optional for Fall 2025 and Fall 2026 applicants. English Proficiency Testing is required if applicable. Portfolios are required or optional for specific programs, but not for the Bachelor of Arts in Cinema & Media Studies.
Description: The BA in Cinema & Media Studies offers students a critical and theoretical understanding of moving images and screen cultures across different media platforms, historical periods, and national contexts. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including the history of cinema, television studies, digital media, critical theory, and the political economy of media industries. Students develop analytical skills to interpret and evaluate cinematic and media texts, explore the social, cultural, and political impact of media, and engage with contemporary debates in the field. The program prepares students for various careers in media industries, arts and culture organizations, education, and graduate studies in cinema and media studies or related humanities fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application (including BU Member Questions and Essays), an Application Fee, Secondary School Report, Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, and Teacher Evaluation. SAT or ACT scores are optional for the 2024–2025 application cycle. English Proficiency Exam Scores are required if applicable.
Description: A deep investigation of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds through their material and literary cultures, with a focus on historical study. Students pursuing a BA in Classical Studies with a concentration in Classical Archaeology explore archaeology, art history, history, languages, literature, and culture from the Bronze Age through Late Antiquity. This concentration combines archaeological fieldwork, museum studies, and advanced study in art history and history with intensive language training and literary studies. Students engage with the intellectual, political, and social history of the classical world and its material remains from the Mediterranean and Near East.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science
Requirements: We are committed to making the application process as clear and straightforward as possible. Here's a breakdown of what you'll need to submit to be considered for first-year admission: Common Application or Coalition Application; BU Questions (Supplement to the Common Application or Coalition Application. Please answer the short answer questions.); Official High School Transcript(s); Counselor Recommendation and School Report; Teacher Recommendation; Standardized Test Scores (SAT or ACT) (optional for students applying for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, and Fall 2026 admission); English Proficiency Test Scores (if English is not your first language, you are required to submit official results from either the TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test (DET)); Midyear Grade Report; Application Fee or Fee Waiver; Interview (Optional); Portfolio (Required for Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, and Pardee School of Global Studies).
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Computer Science in the College of Arts & Sciences provides students with a broad education in the liberal arts and a major in computer science. The program trains students in the fundamental principles and practical applications of computing while allowing them to develop expertise in other subjects and explore new interests. A major in computer science provides students with an education in the principles and applications of computing. Through coursework, students develop the skills needed to design, implement, and analyze computational solutions to problems across a range of applications. The BA program provides a robust foundation in computer science and also allows students to pursue interests in other fields by giving them greater flexibility in their curriculum.

ProgramName: Minor in Core Curriculum
Requirements: To declare a minor in the Core Curriculum, please contact College of Arts & Sciences (CAS) Advising to speak with an advisor.
Description: The BU Core Curriculum offers a unique opportunity to engage with many of Boston University’s best teachers, explore timeless questions about justice, truth, good, and evil, and form close intellectual relationships with other students. The Core minor allows students to earn minor credit for work they are already doing in the Core or to extend their Core experience beyond the four-semester sequence.

ProgramName: Minor in Core Independent Studies
Requirements: Students may declare the Core Minor at any point during their undergraduate career. No special application is necessary; students simply declare the Minor through the MyBU Student Portal.
Description: The Core Curriculum is designed to broaden students’ intellectual horizons, introduce them to major fields of inquiry, and foster an appreciation of the enduring questions of human existence. The Core offers an interdisciplinary approach to the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences through team-taught courses and a cohort-based experience for the first two years. A minor in Core Independent Studies requires a minimum of five (5) courses (20 credits) and is open to all students at Boston University.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Earth & Environment
Requirements: Required materials for first-year applicants include: Application (Common Application or Coalition Application, including essay questions), Application Fee or Fee Waiver, Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, and Standardized Test Scores (optional for applicants applying for fall 2024). Optional materials include an Arts Supplement and Alumni Interview.
Description: Our BA in Earth & Environment program offers students a broad interdisciplinary training in earth and environmental sciences and their interaction with human society. Graduates are prepared for a variety of professions in fields such as environmental consulting, environmental law, city and regional planning, natural resource management, and environmental education. Many graduates also pursue advanced degrees in these fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: Applicants are required to submit the Common Application or QuestBridge Application, Essays, Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation & School Report, Teacher Recommendation, and a Midyear Report (if applicable). English Proficiency is required if applicable, and College Transcripts are required if applicable.
Description: As a student pursuing a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Economics, you will become fluent in the tools of economic analysis and develop the quantitative reasoning and data analysis skills increasingly valued in a broad range of occupations. You will learn to apply economic reasoning to analyze and understand social behavior, evaluate public policy, and make sound decisions in business and finance. The BA in Economics provides a strong foundation for employment in business, finance, consulting, and government, and for graduate study in law, business, and public policy, as well as economics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: Common Application or QuestBridge Application, Boston University Questions, Essay, Secondary School Report & Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Evaluation, Standardized Test Scores (SAT/ACT) - Optional for Fall 2024, Fall 2025, Fall 2026, English Proficiency (if applicable).
Description: The Department of English offers a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree program that emphasizes critical thinking, close reading, and effective communication through the study of literature. Students explore a wide range of literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches, developing skills in analysis, interpretation, and persuasive writing. Our curriculum is designed to foster a deep understanding of literary history and cultural contexts, while also encouraging students to engage with contemporary literary debates and creative practices. Graduates are well-prepared for careers in fields such as education, publishing, journalism, law, marketing, and public relations, or for continued graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Studies
Requirements: Common Application or QuestBridge Application, BU Questions, High School Transcript, Standardized Test Scores (Optional), Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Evaluation, Midyear Report (if applicable), Application Fee or Fee Waiver.
Concentration: German Studies and Russian & East European Studies
Description: The BA in European Studies offers students an interdisciplinary liberal arts education that focuses on the cultures, economies, history, politics, and languages of Europe. The program draws on faculty and courses in the Departments of Classical Studies, Economics, History, Modern Languages & Comparative Literature, Political Science, and Philosophy, as well as the Pardee School of Global Studies. Students achieve proficiency in an official European language and write a capstone senior thesis. Students choose a concentration in either German Studies or Russian & East European Studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Medieval Studies
Requirements: Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, BU-specific Questions and Essay, Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, SAT/ACT Scores (Optional), English Proficiency Exam (if applicable), Midyear Report, and Application Fee or Fee Waiver.
Department: Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies and College of Arts & Sciences
Description: Global Medieval Studies (GMS) is a truly interdisciplinary program that approaches the Middle Ages not as a 'dark age' between two golden ages, but rather as an exciting and formative period of global history. Our program brings together faculty from across Boston University to offer courses that highlight the interconnectedness of different world regions—from Europe and the Mediterranean to Africa, Asia, and the Americas—during the premodern era (roughly 500-1500 CE). In our courses, students explore the cultures, societies, religions, politics, and environments of the global Middle Ages. Students learn to critically analyze various primary sources (texts, artifacts, images, music) and engage with diverse methodologies from different disciplines (history, art history, literature, musicology, religion, philosophy, archaeology, etc.). Through their studies, students develop strong analytical, research, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: First-Year Application Checklist: Common Application or Coalition Application, BU Questions, Essay (on the Common App or Coalition App), Official High School Transcript, Counselor Recommendation, Teacher Recommendation, Midyear School Report (if applying Regular Decision), TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo English Test (if English is not your primary language)
Description: The Department of History emphasizes historical analysis and research skills, enabling students to evaluate arguments, weigh evidence, analyze problems, and craft persuasive arguments. Students gain a deep understanding of historical forces that have shaped the contemporary world, and they develop capacities for critical analysis, research, and communication that are applicable to a wide range of careers. History majors at BU develop: A deep understanding of the historical forces that have shaped the contemporary world; A capacity for critical historical analysis and research across different periods and cultures; The ability to evaluate arguments, weigh evidence, analyze problems, and craft persuasive arguments; and Skills in research, critical thinking, and communication that prepare them for a diverse range of careers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art & Architecture
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, you’ll need to submit the following materials through either the Common Application or the Coalition Application: Common Application or Coalition Application, including the Common Application Personal Essay and BU Questions; Official High School Transcript; Counselor Recommendation & School Report; Teacher Recommendation; Standardized Test Scores (Optional for Fall 2024 and 2025); English Proficiency Exam Scores (if applicable).
Description: Art history provides insight into the history of human culture. Courses address issues of aesthetics, meaning, function, patronage, conservation, and display in the visual arts, as well as the history of architecture and urbanism around the world. As a discipline, art history engages with areas ranging from anthropology to computer science. Our students develop visual, historical, and critical literacy and the communication and research skills necessary to pursue a wide array of careers in the arts and beyond. Through the study of art and architecture, students cultivate a global perspective, a critical understanding of both historical and contemporary societies, and an appreciation for the impact of cultural heritage.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Trustee Scholarship, Presidential Scholarship, National Merit Scholarship
